Besides the content of the various configuration files these settings are needed:

```
arc.conf
  selector_map = "%selector_map_path";
```


top_10.title: Check required inputs before long agent runs
top_10.body:
## Problem

Long agent runs can start without all required inputs. Text may arrive while images or other attachments do not.

The run can then complete against incomplete evidence.

Katie Parrott’s [early-access Fable 5.2 review](https://every.to/vibe-check/fable-5-2) reports an overnight agent run that analyzed slide text but missed deck screenshots. This is an observation, not an independently verified benchmark.

## Change

Add a preflight that inventories required inputs before a long EGM run begins.

The preflight must confirm that the agent can read each required input. It must distinguish text, images, and other attachments.

Stop the run with an actionable error when a required input is absent or unreadable.

## Acceptance criteria

- The run defines its required inputs before execution.
- The preflight confirms the count, type, and identity of each input.
- The preflight verifies that the agent can read each input.
- The run stops before execution when a required input is absent or unreadable.
- The run records the preflight result.
- Automated tests cover text-only input, mixed text and images, a missing image, and an unreadable attachment.

top_10.title: Flaky: test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt (fixed 60 ms sleep before reading flushed frame)
top_10.body:
`test/test_subagent_scale_batch.py::TestCoalescer::test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt` failed on an unrelated PR.

- Run: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/41797479802/job/126467561880 (PR #29490, head 712e6f822c65)
- OS: ubuntu, Python 3.12, Backend Tests shard 3
- Failing line: `((etype, data),) = all_frames` -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)`

The test waits a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.06)` past the 20 ms flush tick and then expects one frame. On a slow runner the flush has not happened yet, so the list is empty. It passes 8/8 locally (alone and with the whole file under -n 4). PR #29490 does not touch the coalescer or this test.

Likely fix: wait for the frame (poll with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

top_10.title: Church name text hidden in sidebar but still shown on login page when a custom logo is uploaded
top_10.body:
## Description When a custom church logo is uploaded (Admin → System → Church Information), the church-name text is hidden in the sidebar but still shown on the login page — inconsistent behavior across the two surfaces that both render the logo. - **Sidebar** (`src/Include/Header.php`, lines ~186-199): the `navbar-brand-text` span is wrapped in `if (ChurchLogoService::hasCustomLogo())` — it only renders when there's **no** custom logo: ```php 'navbar-brand-image crm-brand-logo']) ?> ... ``` - **Login page** (`src/session/templates/begin-session.php`, lines 30-37): `ChurchLogo::img()` and `ChurchMetaData::getChurchName()` render unconditionally as separate elements, with no `hasCustomLogo()` check at all: ```php

``` Confirmed identical on both `master` and the `7.8.1` tag (same blob SHA on `begin-session.php` across both refs). The sidebar's hide-on-custom-logo behavior was intentional per #9719 ("The uploaded logo replaces the ChurchCRM branding in the sidebar (where it also hides the church-name text)") on the assumption that an uploaded logo already contains the church name as artwork. The login page not following the same rule means that assumption isn't applied consistently — admins who want the name visible lose it in the sidebar but keep it on login, with no way to choose. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Admin → System → Church Information → upload a custom logo. 2. Visit the dashboard — sidebar shows only the logo, no church name. 3. Log out and view the login page — logo **and** church name are both shown. ## Expected Consistent behavior between the sidebar and the login page — either both hide the name when a custom logo is present, or neither does. ## Reported by maestrovivo, in the project's Discord #support-chat.

issues.title: HLSL output writes the `length()` of a `buffer float*` helper parameter as `v.length()`, which DXC rejects
Docs: stale statements about the chat screen, dictation and image intake found in the chat-ui test campaign
issues.body:
The chat-ui test campaign (PR #741) found these while checking what the docs say against the code. Line numbers are at the campaign's merge base.

- [ ] **rag-design.md ~:666** names a `scopeChipLabel` helper that does not exist; the "Answering from" label is computed inline in `ScopePopover.tsx` (~:240-280).
- [x] **rag-design.md §15.5 / §15.7 (~:2458-2464, ~:2539)** still describe the pre-D69 meter: a "Context: 6.4k / 8k" tooltip and a progressbar with `aria-valuetext`. Today it is a `role="meter"` labelled "Memory" with a "… % full (about 6.4k of 8k tokens)" tooltip (`ContextMeter.tsx`). (PR #776: both now describe the `role="meter"` "Memory" meter and its bands)
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:2377** (Voice dictation) says the "not installed" mic deep-links with `onNavigate('models')`; since #527 it is `models:voice` (`ChatScreen.tsx` ~:2681).
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:12739** (Image understanding §5) says decode "re-encodes to the input MIME"; since #124 a WEBP becomes PNG (`decode.ts` `outputMimeFor`, ~:111; §11 already says so).
- [ ] **Code comments:** `renderer/lib/displayMap.ts` ~:146-148 repeats the "lands on an odd index" claim that #741 corrected in AssistantMarkdown (with one capture group the split always ends on prose), and `shared/citation-markers.ts` ~:18 and displayMap say `normalizeMathDelimiters` lives in Transcript.tsx (it is in AssistantMarkdown.tsx).
- [x] **ChatScreen.tsx ~:1834-1836**: the stream `finally` comment promises the "Stopped" toast only when no error explained the early end; the condition never reads the error (see #742). (PR #776: the condition now reads `sendSucceeded`, and the comment says why)

issues.title: fix(ci): migrate reusable eval workflows to the Go CLI and require real automatic-run artifacts
issues.body:
## Summary

<!-- 2-4 sentences: describe the bug, feature request, documentation gap, or task. -->

The reusable `waza.yaml` workflow still installs a Python package and uses obsolete CLI/result contracts, while automatic `waza-eval.yml` runs do not resolve output defaults before execution. A successful current-main automatic evaluation run uploaded no result artifact. Migrate retained consumer workflows and examples to one tested Go CLI contract; proposed target v0.41.0.

## Type of issue

- [x] Bug
- [ ] Feature request
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Maintenance
- [ ] Question or investigation

## Agent instructions

<!-- Make this actionable for a coding agent. Include constraints, likely files, and what not to change. -->

- Goal: Every advertised reusable workflow invokes the actual Go Waza contract, preserves meaningful failures, and produces usable evidence on push/PR/dispatch/call events.
- In scope: Installation/source-version strategy, supported arguments, effective input defaults, result/output mapping, artifact verification, and corresponding CI guide/site examples.
- Out of scope: Reintroducing Python Waza, altering product exit/reporting policies to accommodate stale examples, silently changing callers' output names, or using mutable latest installs as exact-source regression evidence.
- Likely files or areas: `.github/workflows/waza.yaml`, `waza-eval.yml`, `skills-ci-example.yml`, `docs/CI-CD-GUIDE.md`, site CI documentation and workflow contract tests.
- Dependencies or related issues: Coordinate final enforcement with [#900](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/900). Keep reporter product bug [#892](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/issues/892) separate; this issue fixes workflow consumption and result evidence, not the reporter implementation.

## Current behavior

<!-- What happens today? For bugs, include the actual result and error output if available. -->

[`waza.yaml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza.yaml#L48-L81) runs `pip install waza`, `--format json`, `--fail-threshold`, `waza report`, and reads `.summary.pass_rate` / `.summary.composite_score`. Current Go run accepts `default` or `github-comment` output format and writes native summary fields such as `success_rate`; there is no corresponding `cmd_report.go` command. In [`waza-eval.yml`](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/blob/f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c/.github/workflows/waza-eval.yml#L154-L197), `OUTPUT_FILE` reads a raw input that is empty on automatic events, but upload falls back to `results.json`. [Current-main run 41918346222](https://github.com/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222) succeeded, warned `No files were found with the provided path: results.json`, and its artifacts API returned an empty list. The CI guide repeats obsolete summary keys/actions, so documentation can propagate the mismatch.

## Expected behavior

<!-- What should happen instead? For feature requests, describe the desired outcome. -->

Resolve effective defaults once for all event types and use the same values for execution, parsing, summary, and upload. Use a reviewed Go installation/build strategy with genuine embedded dashboard assets where source builds require them. Validate result shape, completeness, and availability instead of interpreting null/missing values as zero or success. Preserve documented reusable inputs/outputs through migration or explicitly document reviewed breaking changes.

## Steps to reproduce

<!-- For bugs, provide the smallest reproducible example. Delete if not applicable. -->

1. Inspect the historical Python workflow against `cmd/waza/cmd_run.go` and `internal/models/outcome.go` at the cited SHA.
2. Read the current-main automatic run log's artifact warning.
3. Query `GET /repos/microsoft/waza/actions/runs/41918346222/artifacts` and compare the empty list with the workflow's stated result-artifact contract.

## Environment

<!-- Fill in what you know. Delete fields that are not relevant. -->

- OS: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
- Waza version or commit: `f5789f75fa00924411734d07fd4012ba80e2154c`.
- Go version: CI specifies 1.26; stale reusable workflow provisions Python 3.11.
- Command run: Read-only `gh run view 41918346222 --log`, artifacts API, and local CLI/model source reads.

## Acceptance criteria

<!-- Use checkboxes so an agent can verify completion directly. -->

- [ ] Retained reusable workflows install/build the intended Go version and invoke supported commands and flags.
- [ ] Push, PR, workflow_dispatch, and workflow_call paths resolve identical defaults; explicit custom output/context inputs remain intact.
- [ ] Actual CLI fixtures cover passing grading, completed failing grading, task/runtime errors, missing/malformed artifacts, zero scores, and absent values without success-shaped fallbacks.
- [ ] Automatic successful runs must upload a fresh, complete result artifact; missing evidence fails rather than only warning.
- [ ] Workflow outputs and thresholds use validated current producer fields and preserve failure exit policy.
- [ ] Copied CI guide/site workflows are exercised by contract tests against actual CLI help and saved JSON; unsupported legacy actions/installation examples are migrated or explicitly retired.

## Validation expectations

<!-- List expected automated or manual checks, or say why validation is not applicable. -->

- [ ] Applicable `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `golangci-lint run`.
- [ ] `NO_COLOR=1 make test-compat` for behavior-affecting workflow/CLI contracts.
- [ ] Docs site checked, if docs changed: build and Chromium e2e; documentation example controls execute copied commands.
- [ ] Web/dashboard checks run, if `web/` changes.
- [ ] Other: event/default mutation controls and production-CLI fixture runs with a rejecting offline runtime; verify actual uploaded artifact content on current-head CI.

## Additional context

<!-- Add links, screenshots, logs, related issues, or implementation notes. -->

Research date: 2026-11-06. The Python workflow was identified statically; no third-party Python package was installed or executed. The missing automatic-run artifact is directly observed, not inferred.

issues.title: [Request] 文档：Secure Boot 开启下的自签流程（db 自签 / MOK+shim）与三个已知坑
issues.body:
> 起草说明：本文由 AI 辅助整理，事实来自仓库现状与 #145 的讨论；**没有做真机验证**（我这台没有可切 Secure Boot 的独显机位），凡未实测之处都已标注。若与现场不符，以现场为准。

### 建议类型 / Request type

文档修正 / Documentation change

### 当前问题与需求 / Current problem and need

**要解决的是文档缺口，不是功能缺口。** 想让 Secure Boot 保持开启的用户，现在在文档里只能读到一句：

- `docs/faq.md:272` / `docs/faq.en.md:263`：`替换 U 盘启动文件前先备份。Secure Boot 关闭或使用受信任的自签 EFI。`

这句话承认了自签这条路存在，但没有过程。而 [#145](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/145)（已关闭）里三条路只写全了一条：

| #145 里的方案 | 文档状态 |
|---|---|
| 方案一 休眠切换法（SB 开/关来回切） | 评论里有完整流程，未入 FAQ |
| 方案二 固件内置 FFS（PR #100） | `docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162` 有可行性，标注【待实证】 |
| 方案三 MOK + shim | 评论里有六步，未入 FAQ |
| 方案三 db 自签 | **只有"简版"一句**：每台机器手动导证书、每次更新重签 |

而现场反馈指向的恰恰是最后这条：#145 里有一条西语报告——"Conseguí firmar con un certificado propio el Efi, de modo que ha sido posible iniciar con el secure boot activado"（用自己的证书签了 EFI，因此可以在 Secure Boot 开启下启动）。这是 db 自签路线**可用**的现场证据，但它现在埋在一条已关闭的 issue 的评论区里，既没进 FAQ，也没进兼容性记录。

现实需求面也不小：#145 的原始动机是打 LoL/Vanguard（反作弊要求 SB 开启），而 `docs/community-reports.md` 里的实测行几乎每条都写着 "Secure Boot off"——SB-on 场景目前是文档空白区。

补充一点定位：这**不是**在申请"绕过 Secure Boot"。自签属 `SECURITY.md:53` 威胁模型里"已开启 Secure Boot 且已导入自签证书"的合法配置，与方案一、方案二并列，只是缺文档。

### 期望改进 / Desired improvement

新增 `docs/faq.md#secureboot`（EN 同步 `docs/faq.en.md`）一节，建议内容：

1. **两条路线对比表**：db 自签（固件直接验你的签名，代价是每台导证 + 每次重签）vs MOK+shim（不动 db，走发行版 shim）。shim 那条直接链接 #145 现有六步，不重复写。
2. **db 自签五步**：
   - 生成密钥/证书（`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -addext "extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning"`——这个 EKU 不能省，Windows 侧 `signtool` 会校验）；
   - 签名与验证（`sbsign --key ... --cert ... --output ...`；`sbverify --cert ...`；Windows 等价物 `signtool sign /fd SHA256` + `signtool verify /pa`）；
   - 把 **DER 证书追加**进 db 的三种方式：固件 Key Management（`db → Append / Append from file`）、`efitools` 的 `efi-updatevar -a -c cert.crt -k KEK.key db`、`sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft`（`--microsoft` 才会把微软证书一并写回）；
   - 新版 maker 直接吃签名后的件：`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284`（`-BootEfi`）、`:488`（盘根）、`:494`（`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`），即
     ```powershell
     .\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family ad102 -Out G:\ -BootEfi .\BOOTX64.signed.efi
     ```
   - 验证：`mokutil --sb-state` 应为 `SecureBoot enabled`；固件层真正放行的铁证是盘上出现新的 `loader.log` 且含 `TX BUILD` banner。
3. **三条硬纪律**（这部分比签名本身更容易出事）：
   - **只能追加，不能替换 db 里的微软证书**——`bootmgfw.efi` 靠 *Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011* 签名，删了 Windows 起不来；
   - **动 PK 前先导出 PK/KEK/db 备份**；若板子要求清 PK 进 Setup Mode 才能 Append，事后必须把原厂证书恢复并重新 enroll PK；
   - **私钥只留本机**：db 里一旦有你的证书，这把私钥就能给这台机器签任何引导组件。
4. **三个已知坑**：
   - **SB 开着时 `ssdiag` 仍然不可用**：它临时加载的 `pmxdrv.sys` 是 Intel/COMODO 2018 交叉签名、无微软根，SB-ON 必然被 DSE 拒（`tools/ssdiag/README.md` 的 "Secure Boot — the gate that actually refuses this driver"、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`）。所以 SB 常开的机器上，系统内读回只能走 `loader.log` 的 `HANDOFF-OUT`（EFI 阶段零驱动读回）或 Linux 侧 `tools/diag-unlock.py`；要 `ssdiag --reapply` 修回锁，仍须临时关一次 SB。
   - **BitLocker / PCR[7]**：SB 或 db 状态变化会改 PCR[7]，可能弹恢复密钥，操作前先挂起保护。
   - **换版本必须重签**，签名后再改一个字节即失效；资产 `*.bin` 不需要签名（SB 只验 PE 引导链）。
5. **反作弊边界**（与 #145 的警告保持一致）：db 自签不改 SB 状态位，Vanguard（LoL）通常可过；ACE 系（腾讯）会校验 TPM/PCR[7] 链式启动记录，自签链的度量与原厂引导不同，**不保证过检**——打 ACE 系游戏请回到方案一。

顺带把 `docs/faq.md:272` / `.en.md:263` 那句改成带锚点的链接。

### 相关版本、文档与参考资料 / Versions, documentation and references

- 文档现状：`docs/faq.md:272`、`docs/faq.en.md:263`（自签仅一句）
- 讨论：#145（休眠切换法、FFS 方案、MOK+shim 六步、db 自签简版）；西语现场反馈在该 issue 评论中
- 固件形态可行性：`docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162`（SB 只验 OS 引导链）
- maker 的 boot 路径改动：`5684752`（打印可执行 copy 步骤）、`c0f3518`（输出不再纯平铺）、`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284/488/494/500/505-511`
- ssdiag 的 SB 门：`tools/ssdiag/README.md`、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`
- 威胁模型定位：`SECURITY.md:53`
- FAQ 判据/回锁值（本 issue 不涉及，仅说明读回路径不同）：`docs/faq.md:189`、`docs/cold-values.md:139`

### 替代方案与补充信息 / Alternatives and additional context

- **替代**：维持现状，让每个 SB-on 用户自己在 Discussions 问一遍。现状的代价是 #145 已经被关掉，新来的人搜不到过程。
- **更小的一步**：只把这份内容作为 #145 的补充评论贴回去——但该单已关闭，不解决"下次还能找到吗"。
- **我愿意直接出 patch**：如果维护者认可，可以照 #141 / #144 的方式提 docs PR，中英同步、只动 `docs/faq*.md`。
- **缺一个现场字段**：能否请 #145 那位西语报告者补 **主板型号** 与 **`ssdiag` 是否被拒**（第 4 条里"必然被拒"还是"通常被拒"取决于此），以及 **BitLocker 是否弹过恢复密钥**。这三项决定文档该写成硬性结论还是保守表述。

issues.title: [Report] RTX 4060 Laptop (28A0) / MECHREVO Yaoshi15Pro 2024 (GM5IX0A, i7-14650HX) - v2.1.9 TX success, matched A/B FP16 +81%, 15-inch thin laptop @ 140 W
issues.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

`10de:28a0`（AD107 · 24 SM · 8 GB）在机械革命 **耀世15Pro 2024**（i7-14650HX / 32 GB）上完成 **v2.1.9 Ada 事务**，EFI 侧读回全绿（`HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff`），Windows 正常进入。

**平台定位需要先说明**：这是一台 **15 寸轻薄游戏本**，不是同 TGP 的厚砖机。140 W 塞进这个厚度的机身，散热余量本来就是这个形态的短板——下面的 87 ℃ / 2.5 GHz 持续数据要放在这个前提下看，不代表其他 140 W 机型的水平。

同一脚本、同一 GPU 设置（140 W / 核心 +105 MHz / 显存 +200 MHz）的前后对照：

| 路径 | 解锁前 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.26 / 21.27 | **38.45** | **+81%** |
| BF16 | 21.25 / 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 / 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3 | 40.79 / 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（对照） | 6.41 / 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

绝对值比 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）和 [#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882）低 13–15%，实测受 **140 W 功耗墙 + 87 ℃ 温度墙**限制（持续负载下核心 2625 → 2430 MHz），与这台 15 寸轻薄机身的散热包络相符。新增信息：28a0 的首份**同脚本匹配 A/B**，以及解锁态下的持续功耗/时钟/温度采样。

---

## 工具版本 / Tool version

- **nv-uefi-unlocker v2.1.9** 官方发布包，未做任何本地修改
- `BOOTX64.EFI` 335,872 B，SHA-256 `9D2C41F90B290AD0DA3ECF294016A7EA67638E2625D8E1B1735028298943BB5C`（与 [#35](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/35) 记录的官方 v2.1.9 同一文件）
- 资产：`-Family 40` 生成的 `ad102` family 共 8 个文件，`loader.log` 中逐个 `TX-ASSET-DIAG: ... loaded N/N bytes` 全量校验通过
- 未使用 `i_know_what_i_am_doing.txt` / `tx-quiet.txt` / `tx-select-bdf.txt` / `tx-require-d0.txt` 等任何 marker（日志中均为 `absent`）

## GPU 与平台 / GPU and platform

- **GPU**：NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU，AD107，24 SM，8192 MiB
- **PCI ID**：`10DE:28A0`，子系统 `139A:1D05`（机械革命），地址 `0000:01:00.0`；音频功能 `10de:22be @ 01:00.1`
- **VBIOS**：`95.07.3f.00.26`　**驱动**：596.49（WDDM）
- **整机**：MECHREVO **耀世15Pro 2024**（Yaoshi15Pro Series GM5IX0A），**15 寸轻薄游戏本**；Intel Core i7-14650HX；内存 32 GB
- **BIOS**：American Megatrends International `N.1.05MRO06`（2024-01-30）
- **OS**：Windows 11 Pro build 26200
- **显示拓扑**：**独显直连**，内屏由 dGPU 驱动，2560×1440 @ 240 Hz；Intel UHD Graphics 存在于系统中但无显示输出（`CM_PROB_PHANTOM`），无 eGPU、无第二块独立显卡
- **功耗档**：机械革命电竞控制台「狂飙」档，`ConfigurableTGPSwitch=1 / ConfigurableTGPTarget=140`、Dynamic Boost 开关关闭（值 25）、核心 +105 MHz、显存 +200 MHz；实测 `power.draw` 峰值 139.8 W
- **启动方式**：UEFI，AMI F7 一次性启动菜单，FAT32 U 盘（VendorCo ProductCode，MBR，63 GB 中划 30 GB 分区）
- **Secure Boot**：事务时**已关闭**（当前仍未恢复）；**CSM / ReBAR：未检查**

## 操作过程 / Procedure

1. 在目标机（本机）解压 v2.1.9 发布包，管理员 PowerShell 运行 `.\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family 40`，自动识别本机为 40 系并只生成 `ad102` 资产；`NVIDIA-kernel-module-source-610.43.03` 与 `nvidia-utils-610.43.03` 两个钉版输入按脚本校验通过
2. 把脚本列出的 7 个 `.bin` 复制到 U 盘根目录，`BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`
3. BIOS 中关闭 Secure Boot；从系统「重启」→ F7 一次性菜单选 `UEFI: VendorCo ProductCode 1.00, Partition 1`
4. 版本屏按 **空格** 确认（无 armed marker，走 30 秒超时语义）
5. 事务完成后自动链回 Windows，未修改 NVRAM 永久启动顺序
6. 全程只尝试了这一次事务，无重试、无断电恢复过程

## EFI 执行结果 / EFI execution result

```
TX: ===== target 1/1: 10de:28a0 @ 0000:01:00.0 =====
TX: device 10de:28a0 -> asset family 'ad102'
TX: V67 present - unlock mode (family-specific write chain)
TX: BEGIN (phases: detach claim pre-flr scrub gfw layout fwsec booter verify selectors restore flr)
TX: >4GB staging gate: false (family ad102)
TX: detach+claim ok
POST-BOOT: FEAT_PLM=0xffffffff SS0=0x161166 SS1=0x5
POST-BOOT: FACTORY FEAT_READOUT_1=0x00410080 (0 = full speed; badf5040 = PLM still closed)
POST-BOOT: SEC2 MAILBOX0=0x67b00001 WPR2_HI=0x1ffae00
POST-BOOT: WPRCFG=0xfffff0ff FBPA=0xffffff0f WPR=0xffffffff
SELECTOR RESULT: SS0=0x88888888 SS1=0x8
POST-FLR: GFW halted the cores
POST-FLR: WPR2=0x1ffffe00/0x0
POST-FLR: verified (selectors survive AON)
RECONNECT: ConnectController ok (recursive=true)          ← 默认 recursive=true，未跳过重连
FINAL: transaction complete, all DMA released
SELECTOR RESULT: transaction complete
HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff wpr2_hi=0x0
             pmcsr=0x0008 dstate=D0 | tu10x: ... | tu10x_unlock=false ss0_unlock=true ss1_unlock=true plm_open=true
CHAIN-PRE: start-time PE header probe ok - StartImage the preloaded '\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi'
```

阶段时序（`[+ms]` 前缀）：CONFIRM 262ms → 空格 14527ms → 事务本体 19300ms 起 → FINAL 22704ms → CHAIN 22799ms。

补充读回：事务前采样的 `SAMPLE FEAT_READOUT_1 = 0x00410080` 与 `POST-BOOT: FACTORY FEAT_READOUT_1=0x00410080` 一致，与本仓 [cold-values.md](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/blob/main/docs/cold-values.md) 已载的 AD107 出厂值逐位相同（九个 3 位字段中 #2/#5/#7 = 2），解锁后 `HANDOFF-OUT` 读到 `0x00000000`——与既有 AD107 冷值表吻合，不构成新数据点。

## 系统内验证 / In-OS verification

- Windows 正常启动，`bootmgfw` 链回成功，无 Code 12、无黑屏、无 TDR
- 驱动 596.49 正常加载，`nvidia-smi` 列出 GPU 于 `00000000:01:00.0`，P0，`Disp.A On`（独显直连持有显示）
- PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 正常运算，所有基准正确性检查 PASS
- **ssdiag：未通过，因此独立寄存器读回未验证。** 具体输出：

```
PLATFORM: vulnerable-driver blocklist = OFF
PLATFORM: core isolation (HVCI)       = unknown (value absent - the Windows default applies)
PLATFORM: Secure Boot                 = OFF
NOTE: a signed kernel driver is installed for the duration of the probe; ...
StartService failed: win32 31
```

  `SSDIAG_PMXDRV` 服务已成功安装（System 日志 7045，`\??\C:\Users\...\Temp\ssdiag-pmxdrv.sys`），但启动返回 `ERROR_GEN_FAILURE`。HVCI 场景键在本机注册表中不存在、VBS 未启用，**看起来不是代码完整性拦截**，暂按 [#40](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/40) 说的「平台拒绝 vs 驱动不能干活」两类形态无法区分，尚未复跑。系统侧状态目前仅由 EFI `HANDOFF-OUT` 读回 + 吞吐签名两方面佐证。

## 原始证据 / Raw evidence

- 完整 `loader.log`（433 行 / 40,719 B）见文末折叠块，未经修改
- `tools/collect_compat.py` 输出：`gpus=2 fields=46 verdicts=15`，`10de:28a0` 判为 `ad102 (Ada)`。注意它把音频功能 `10de:22be` 也列成了一个 GPU 条目（两条记录字段完全相同），不确定是否符合预期
- 无 NVIDIA 固件、无 BitLocker 密钥、无序列号；`loader.log` 已按 CONTRIBUTING 要求检查过

## 性能对比 / Performance comparison

**口径**：`make-usbroot.ps1` 自带前的自写脚本 `gemm_bench.py`（`torch.mm`，8192 系尺寸扫，`cudaEvent` 计时，每尺寸 5 次预热 + 3 窗口 × 20 次取中位），**解锁前后同脚本、同 GPU 设置**；解锁前为上一次启动（stock），解锁后为事务后同一次启动，两次测量间隔约 40 分钟，期间未改任何 GPU 设置。

**A/B（N=4096，TF/s）**

| 路径 | stock 第1次 | stock 第2次 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.27 | 21.26 | **38.45** | +81% |
| BF16 | 21.25 | 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 | 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3（`_scaled_mm`） | 40.79 | 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（TF32 off，对照） | 6.41 | 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 153.0 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

`FP16 / FP8` 比值：stock 0.52 → 解锁后 0.51；`FP16 / FP32` 比值：stock 3.1× → 解锁后 5.9×。三条对照（FP32、显存带宽、以及时钟本身）都持平，说明增益不是时钟或散热瞬态造成的。

**其他尺寸（解锁后，同一脚本）**：FP16 1024 → 42.51，4096 → 38.45，8192 → 35.46。

**第二套独立基准交叉验证**：用 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119) 附件里的 `baseline-gemm-v1.py` 原样跑（N=4096、`torch.mm(a,b,out=c)`、7 组 × 30 次、每组一个 event 窗口）：**FP16 37.587 TF/s，BF16 38.227 TF/s**，与本机自写脚本的 38.45 / 38.66 一致（差 2%）。

**持续负载（解锁后，FP16 GEMM 4096，连续 40 s）**

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 吞吐 | 36.06 TF/s（40 s 平均） |
| 核心时钟 | 2625 → 2430 MHz，均值 **2545 MHz** |
| 功耗 | 均值 132 W，峰值 **139.8 W**（顶死 140 W TGP） |
| 温度 | 79 → **87 ℃**（控制台 `TargetTemperature` 即为 87） |

**与现有报告的对比（仅供维护者参考，不作结论）**：[#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）stock 29.51 → 44.24；[#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882 桌面）n=4096 FP16 26.98 → 42.44。本机 stock 21.26 明显更低但增益更大（+81% vs +49% / +57%）。解锁后绝对值低 13–15%，而 **每 MHz 效率与 #119 接近**（本机 36.06 / 2545 MHz ≈ 14.2 GFLOPS/MHz；按其 44.24 反推约 3.0 GHz 得 ~14.7），因此**我倾向于认为这是 140 W 笔记本散热包络下的频率差异，而非解锁不完整**——这一条是假设，没有 ssdiag 读回佐证。

## 限制条件与相关记录 / Limitations and related reports

**未验证 / 未测试**

- ssdiag 未跑通（`StartService win32 31`），系统内寄存器读回**未验证**；上面的「非部分解锁」判断属假设
- CSM、ReBAR 未检查
- 未做 nvoc 侧功耗墙解锁组合测试，未测解锁后的降噪/续航影响
- 只做过一次事务，未验证复现性；各状态只测了 1–2 次

**测量条件（可能压低绝对值）**

- 两次测量期间桌面都在 2560×1440 @ 240 Hz 下运行，且有界面在重绘；用 `\GPU Engine(*)\Utilization Percentage` 采样到非基准进程占用 3D 引擎（dwm 约 25% + 前端约 40%）。这会对绝对吞吐有影响，但前后两次条件相同，且 FP32 / 带宽两条对照持平
- 环境温度为室温、无额外散热措施；持续负载下温度 87 ℃ 已是该机温度墙

**新增了什么**

- 兼容性矩阵行 `AD107 · 4060 2882 / 4060 Laptop 28a0 / 4050M 28e1` 里，`28a0` 目前是「全链与 Windows 性能验证通过，满载收益受 TGP 限制」；本报告是该 ID 的首份**同脚本匹配 A/B**，并首次给出该形态下解锁态的持续功耗 / 时钟 / 温度采样，可作为「四堵墙中功耗墙+热墙」的实测例子
- 相关：[#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0 同芯片组）、[#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882 桌面同芯片组）、[#40](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/40)（ssdiag 驱动加载门）

**关于本文**：测量、日志与命令均由本人在本机实际执行；报告文字由 AI 助手协助整理，数据以附件日志和脚本输出为准，本人对内容负责。

---

<details>

issues.title: First time contributing? Start here.
issues.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

issues.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
issues.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

issues.title: [Bug]: Failed external tasks lose their structured results in public and durable records
issues.body:
### Issue Origin

Observed or reproduced in a real environment: a local component reproduction using the production Compile status adapter, external-task executor, TaskTracker, persistent store, and public task query. The storage backend and runtime response are synthetic; no deployed server or model was exercised.

### Bug Description

`CompileSessionStatus.result` is preserved by `CompileService._snapshot()` for failed runs. `ExternalTaskService` then records the error with `TaskTracker.fail()` without passing that result, although `fail()` already supports a structured partial result. The public task query returns `result: null`, including after a fresh tracker reloads the durable record.

This loses failed-run diagnostics such as coverage and source errors. The failure status and error remain correct.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct `CompileSessionStatus(status="failed", stage="failed", error={"code": "COMPILE_INCOMPLETE", "message": "Incomplete output"}, result={"coverage": {"completed": 1, "failed": 1}, "source_errors": ["chapter.md"]})`.
2. Convert it using the production `CompileService._snapshot()` and return it from a registered provider's `on_start` recovery hook.
3. Create a Compile task through `TaskTracker(PersistentTaskStore(...))` with `meta={"request": {}}`, then call `ExternalTaskService.execute()` for its owner.
4. Query through `openviking.server.routers.tasks.get_task()` and reload the same store into a new TaskTracker.

### Expected Behavior

Both public and reloaded records retain the provider's structured result with status `failed` and the original error. Existing TaskTracker result sanitization still applies.

### Actual Behavior

Both records return:

```json
{"status":"failed","result":null,"error":"COMPILE_INCOMPLETE: Incomplete output"}
```

### OpenViking Version

main at `51f0e8e262060e95a897e8480fa9fa47652f75ed`

### Python Version

3.13.9

### Operating System

Windows

### Model Backend

None

### Additional Context

I plan a focused fix at the external-task finalization boundary and regression coverage of polling, recovery, persistence, and public queries in the existing persistent-task restart contract. No new result schema, completion policy, or rollback behavior is proposed.

Related: #7303 discusses partial Compile output and salvage policy. This report only concerns preserving a result when the effective terminal snapshot is already `failed`; it does not implement or decide salvage policy. Searches across open and closed PRs for `snapshot.result`, `ExternalTaskService result`, and external partial results found no equivalent fix.

Investigation and the local reproduction were performed with Codex assistance.

issues.title: [Bug]: ContextArranger ignores live node metadata and timeout drift
issues.body:
### Issue Origin

Observed or reproduced locally through the public Python SDK with a stateful HTTP fixture. No deployed server or external MCP tool was used.

### Bug Description

After a live node is applied, remounting it with the same tool, arguments, and ownership tags but a different title, description, or timeout leaves `ContextArranger.plan()` reporting `UNCHANGED`. `apply()` then sends no update, so the declaration cannot restore the node's intended metadata or execution timeout.

The server's `MCPService.mount()` persists all three fields and `MCPService.mounts()` returns them. The SDK's `_matches_applied()` compares only the tool URI and arguments after checking the tags. A specification tag describes the last declaration; it cannot establish that these actual mount fields still match.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
arranger = AsyncContextArranger(client, "demo")
arranger.live_context(
    "weather.md", "viking://agent/tools/weather/current.json", "Weather",
    description="Current weather", timeout_seconds=60,
)
await arranger.apply()

await client.mount_mcp_tool(
    "viking://agent/tools/weather/current.json",
    "viking://resources/weather.md", "Changed title",
    description="Changed description", timeout_seconds=5,
    # Keep the existing ownership/specification tags.
)
print((await arranger.plan()).to_dict())
await arranger.apply()
```

The executed reproduction uses the real SDK requests for listing, batch mount, manual mount, and planning, with fixture responses shaped like the corresponding server routes.

### Expected Behavior

The plan reports `UPDATE`; applying it restores the declared title, description, and timeout. A subsequent plan reports `UNCHANGED`.

### Actual Behavior

The plan reports `UNCHANGED`, and apply does not restore the declaration.

### OpenViking Version

main at `51f0e8e262060e95a897e8480fa9fa47652f75ed`

### Python Version

3.13.9

### Operating System

Windows

### Model Backend

None

### Additional Context

I plan to compare these existing mount fields at the current SDK reconciliation boundary and add public SDK convergence coverage. No server schema, ownership rule, API option, or dependency change is needed. Searches of open and closed issues/PRs for ContextArranger and arranger drift found the original feature #6263, but no repair for this behavior.

Investigation and reproduction were performed with Codex assistance.

issues.title: [Bug]: Markdown image deduplication drops equivalent source references
issues.body: ### Issue Origin Observed or reproduced locally using a real Markdown file, a generated PNG, the production Markdown parser, and LocalParseOutputStore. No model or deployed server was used. ### Bug Description When a document references one local image through several equivalent paths, `_ingest_local_images()` deduplicates the resolved filesystem path before retaining the original references. Only the first spelling reaches `.image_mappings.json`. After import, the image is copied next to the generated Markdown, but later references such as `./assets/chart.png` remain pointed at the original source directory. The production image rewriter cannot repair them because their mapping entries were discarded. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a valid 64-by-64 PNG at `assets/chart.png` beside `guide.md`. 2. Parse this document using `MarkdownParser.parse(..., parse_output_store=LocalParseOutputStore(...))`: ```markdown # Guide ![first](assets/chart.png) ![second](./assets/chart.png) ``` 3. Inspect the generated `.image_mappings.json`, then run the production image rewrite with that mapping. ### Expected Behavior Copy the image once and map all three original references to the copied file. Rewrite all three references to the final Viking URI. ### Actual Behavior The mapping contains only `{"assets/chart.png": "chart.png"}`. Only one of the three references is rewritten; the other Markdown image and HTML image remain unchanged and receive image-not-found warnings. ### OpenViking Version main at `51f0e8e262060e95a897e8480fa9fa47652f75ed` ### Python Version 3.13.9 ### Operating System Windows ### Model Backend None ### Additional Context I plan to retain every original spelling while copying each resolved image once, and extend the existing local-artifact parser contract to cover generated mappings, image bytes, the artifact manifest, and final rewriting. This concerns mapping creation in the Markdown parser. #6623 concerns retaining an already-created mapping when later rewriting must retry. Searches of open and closed PRs for image aliases, `seen_paths`, image deduplication, and image mappings found no equivalent fix. Investigation and reproduction were performed with Codex assistance.

issues.title: Shared Agent Skills (viking://agent/skills) have no write authorization: any account user key can publish, replace, or delete account-wide skills
issues.body:
### Issue Origin

Observed or reproduced in a real environment

### Bug Description

## 中文

`viking://agent/skills` 是账号级共享技能根目录，但 OpenViking 对它没有任何写权限控制。任何持有同账号有效 `user_key` 的普通用户，都可以通过 `add_skill` 指定 `target_uri=viking://agent/skills` 把 skill 发布给全账号所有用户，也可以静默替换或删除已有共享 skill。

Skill 不是普通文档，而是模型会读取并执行的指令。一个普通用户可以把不成熟、错误甚至恶意的 skill 注入全账号，所有加载共享技能目录的 agent 都可能按它行动。

官方文档要求模型只有用户确认账号级变更后才写入共享区，同名会被 `add_skill` 直接替换。这只是提示词层面的行为约束，不是服务端权限控制；ACL 只支持 `viking://resources`，`viking://agent/skills` 不支持 ACL。

## English

`viking://agent/skills` is the account-wide shared skill root, but OpenViking enforces no write authorization on it. Any ordinary user key in the account can call `add_skill` with `target_uri=viking://agent/skills` to publish a skill to every user, silently replace an existing shared skill, or delete one.

Skills are instructions that agents read and may follow, not passive documents. An ordinary user can inject an immature, incorrect, or malicious skill into the entire account, and every agent that loads the shared catalog can act on it.

The documented requirement to confirm before sharing is prompt-level behavior, not an authorization control. ACL applies only to `viking://resources`, not to `viking://agent/skills`.

### Steps to Reproduce

中文：
1. 使用一个普通用户 key，不需要管理员权限或特殊 ACL；
2. 调用 `add_skill`，传入 `data` 和 `target_uri=viking://agent/skills`；
3. skill 写入 `viking://agent/skills/<name>/`，同账号所有用户可见；
4. 同名再次调用 `add_skill` 会直接替换，不询问；
5. 同一用户也可以删除该共享 skill。

English:
1. Use an ordinary user key with no admin role or special ACL.
2. Call `add_skill` with `data` and `target_uri=viking://agent/skills`.
3. The skill is created at `viking://agent/skills/<name>/` and is visible to every user in the account.
4. Calling `add_skill` again with the same name replaces the shared skill without confirmation.
5. The same user can delete it.

### Expected Behavior

中文：共享技能根目录应支持 ACL，由管理员配置哪些用户/组可写；未配置 ACL 时应默认拒绝写入，而不是让所有普通用户可写。个人技能 `viking://~/skills` 仍归所有者读写。

English: The shared skill root should be ACL-capable, with administrators deciding which users/groups may write. With no ACL configured, writes should fail closed rather than allowing every ordinary user. User-private `viking://~/skills` remains owner-writable.

### Actual Behavior

中文：任何同账号普通用户 key 都可写入、替换、删除共享 skill。尝试设置 ACL 会返回：`ACL is only supported for viking://resources`。

English: Any ordinary user key in the account can write, replace, or delete shared skills. Applying ACL is rejected with: `ACL is only supported for viking://resources`.

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python

```

### Error Logs

```shell

```

### OpenViking Version

0.5.4

### Python Version

3.13

### Operating System

Linux

### Model Backend

None

### Additional Context

建议修复：
1. 让 `viking://agent/skills` 支持 ACL（restricted/inherit、组授权），`add_skill`/`edit`/`write`/`rm` 在服务端做 ACL 校验；
2. 由管理员配置写权限，不硬编码“普通用户只读”；未配置 ACL 时 fail closed；
3. 共享 skill 变更写审计日志（操作者、skill 名、旧/新版本、动作）；
4. ACL 落地前至少对非管理员写入返回 403，或提供账号级白名单；
5. 保留个人技能边界。

Environment: OpenViking 0.5.4, API key auth, ordinary user key, DSH memory plugin exposing mcp__openviking__add_skill.

Request: Please confirm whether unrestricted account-wide skill writes are intentional. If yes, document it as a trust assumption and give clients a supported way to disable the write path; if not, treat it as a security fix rather than a documentation clarification.

issues.title: [Bug] CLI 对 5xx 丢弃服务端 detail，只回 http_5xx_result_unknown
issues.body:
## 用户影响

`memhub` CLI 收到 5xx 时只回一个通用码，服务端已经给出的原因被丢掉。用户无法判断该做什么。

2026-11-06 在一台没有 Secret Service 的 WSL Ubuntu 24.04 上实测：

```
$ memhub models configure --plan-file <plan> --confirm --api-key-file <key>
{"schema_version":1,"product":"memhub","state":"unknown",
 "operation_id":"...","code":"http_503_result_unknown"}
```

同一请求直接打 HTTP，服务端返回：

```json
{"detail":"secure_storage_unavailable"}
```

这是一句可以直接行动的信息：这台机器没有可用的密钥存储。面对 `http_503_result_unknown`，用户无法区分网络问题、参数错误、服务端能力缺失和服务端故障。

## 复现步骤

1. 在没有 Secret Service 的 Linux / WSL 上启动 `one-memory serve`
2. `memhub models configure --plan-file <plan> --confirm --api-key-file <key>`
3. CLI 输出 `http_503_result_unknown`；同一 token 直接 `POST /api/v1/model-profiles` 得到 `{"detail":"secure_storage_unavailable"}`

**说明**：报告时（2026-11-08）该机器已装上可用的密钥存储，无法再现场复现这条 503。上面是 11-06 的原始终端记录；代码路径可在当前 main 上直接核对（见下）。

## 版本与平台

- MemHub 1.0.5，WSL Ubuntu 24.04，无 Secret Service

## 预期与实际结果

**实际**：`core-operations.ts` 的 post / put / patch / delete 四个方法（`:107`、`:162`、`:200`、`:233`）结构相同——4xx 分支调用 `safeErrorCode(response.data, response.status)` 读 body，5xx 分支直接返回 `http_${status}_result_unknown`，不读 body。`safeErrorCode`（`:265`）已实现：从 `body.detail` 取符合 `[a-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}` 的字符串，否则退回 `http_${status}`。`core-client.ts:398` 的 `submitMemoryWrite` 有同样一处。

**现有特例说明这件事已被考虑过**：`core-operations.ts:148-150` 有一段白名单：

```ts
// Core answers a refusal it can name with 503 (`sdk_reembed_unavailable`)
// or 507 (`insufficient_disk_space`) on the switch routes.
([503, 507].includes(response.status) &&
  (EMBEDDING_SWITCH_PATHS as readonly string[]).includes(path))
```

即「503 可能带可读原因」已被认可，但只对 embedding-switch 路径开放。服务端 `_secret_store_detail()`（`api.py:6319`）的 docstring 表达的正是同一诉求：

> "Click Allow", "this is slow, try again", and "there is no store here" are
> three different instructions; sending one string for all of them is why a
> user whose Keychain needs one click was told the store was broken.

**期望**：保持 `state: "unknown"`（5xx 可能已执行一部分，不能报成功），但让 `code` 带上原因，例如 `secure_storage_unavailable_result_unknown`。

## 三种可选实现

| 方案 | 做法 | 取舍 |
|---|---|---|
| **A. 扩大白名单** | 把 `model-profiles` 等已知会返回可命名 5xx 的路径加入 `EMBEDDING_SWITCH_PATHS` 同款清单 | 改动最小，但要逐条维护路径 |
| **B. 所有 5xx 都试读 `detail`** | 5xx 分支读 `body.detail`，读不到退回现有码 | 无需路径清单；需限定字符串形状，避免把地址/路径当成错误码 |
| **C. 维持现状** | 认为 5xx 不该给详情 | 需说明 embedding-switch 为何例外，否则同类问题会反复出现 |

## 隐私确认

- [x] 内容不含密钥、真实对话或个人信息

issues.title: Screensaver quick button never shows on onn 4K Pro (Android 14): the dream package is not visible to the app
issues.body:
**TV:** onn. Streaming Device 4K pro (Google TV, Android 14, API 34)
**couch-tv:** v0.12 release `couch-tv-home.apk`, option A (no bridge), installed with `apply.sh` and `KEEP_AMBIENT=1`
**config:** `"quick": ["screensaver"]`

**What happens:** the home shows no quick buttons at all. The Screensaver button is left out, as if it could not work on this TV.

**Why, as far as I can tell:** `screensaverReady()` in `MainActivity.kt` checks that the dream in `screensaver_components` is enabled with `packageManager.getApplicationInfo(dream.packageName, 0)`. On this box Android's package visibility hides that package from couch-tv, so the call throws and the button is treated as unavailable:

- `dumpsys package queries` says `system apps queryable: false`.
- `com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx` is not force-queryable, and it is not among the packages couch-tv can see (neither "via package name" nor "via component").
- Everything else the check looks at is fine: `appops get app.couchtv.launcher WRITE_SETTINGS` is `allow`, `screensaver_enabled` is `1`, `screensaver_components` is `com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx/.service.Backdrop`, and dreamx is enabled.

The sleep timer's end action (`startAmbientNow()`) does not go through this check, so starting the screensaver itself should work here; only the visibility check fails.

**Possible fix:** let the app see dream services in the manifest's `<queries>`, for example

```xml
<intent><action android:name="android.service.dreams.DreamService" /></intent>
```

which covers whichever dream a TV uses, or `<package android:name="com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx" />`. `openAmbientSettings()` probably has the same problem, since it resolves `dreamx.two.panel.SETTINGS`; an `<intent><action android:name="dreamx.two.panel.SETTINGS" /></intent>` query would cover that. Not tested with a patched build.

Everything else in the option A setup worked on this box: the home, Keep watching from Watch Next, the Home button watch, and the Google TV home and setup app left on.

issues.title: Philips Android TV: the remote's TV/channels key does nothing on the couch-tv home (WebView keeps it)
issues.body:
**TV:** TPV 2021/22 Philips UHD Android TV, Android 11 (API 30), stock home `com.google.android.tvlauncher`. Option A, couch-tv 0.11 from Releases.

**What happens:** With the couch-tv home on screen, the remote's channels (TV) key does nothing. Live TV (Freeview) itself works: `am start -n org.droidtv.playtv/.PlayTvActivity` opens it fine, and so does the Watch TV tile in More apps.

**What I found (over ADB, `input keyevent KEYCODE_TV`):**
- From inside YouTube, logcat shows WindowManager treating it as unhandled, and Philips' global key receiver then acts on it:
  ```
  D/WindowManager: Unhandled key: ATF-1,key=170,KeyEvent { action=ACTION_DOWN, keyCode=KEYCODE_FAC_FAC, scanCode=170, ... }
  D/GlobalKeyRcv: GLOBAL_BUTTON
  ```
  (Philips' build names keycode 170 `KEYCODE_FAC_FAC`; it is `KEYCODE_TV` in AOSP.) The TV then leaves YouTube (on this set it first showed Philips' own consent screen, `org.droidtv.nettvregistration/.onetrust.IABActivity`).
- From the couch-tv home there is no "Unhandled key" line and no `GlobalKeyRcv`: the key never reaches Philips, and couch-tv stays on screen. `KEYCODE_GUIDE` and `KEYCODE_CHANNEL_UP` do nothing either.

So `MainActivity.dispatchKeyEvent` passes these keys to `super.dispatchKeyEvent`, the WebView consumes them, and Philips only handles the TV key as an unhandled-key fallback.

**Suggested fix (not built or tested by me):** in `MainActivity.dispatchKeyEvent`, before `super`, give the TV's own keys back unhandled, for example:

```kotlin
when (event.keyCode) {
    KeyEvent.KEYCODE_TV, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_GUIDE, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_CHANNEL_UP,
    KeyEvent.KEYCODE_CHANNEL_DOWN, KeyEvent.KEYCODE_LAST_CHANNEL,
    KeyEvent.KEYCODE_TV_INPUT -> return false
}
```

Matching by number covers Philips' renamed 170. One caveat: I tested with keys sent over ADB, not by pressing the physical button, though the physical button behaves the same way for the owner (does nothing on the couch-tv home).

Set up with an AI agent (Claude Code), which did the ADB checks above.

issues.title: Add an optional ADB helper for importing photos when the TV picker is broken
issues.body:
Could the repo include an optional computer-side helper for adding local photos on TVs whose document picker is missing or broken?

On my TCL G10 Google TV (Android 14), Couch TV's photo picker resolves to the placeholder `com.android.tv.frameworkpackagestubs` instead of a usable DocumentsUI. I got local photos imported with a reversible ADB workflow: push the selected PNG/JPG files to shared storage, scan them into the media library, temporarily disable the placeholder only if it was originally enabled so Couch TV can open the working system photo picker, then restore the original package state and restart Couch TV after selection. Couch TV copies selected images into its own app storage; they do not need to stay in shared storage.

Would an opt-in tool under `tv-home/tools/` be useful for this case? It could use an existing ADB connection, verify transferred files, and guide the user through selecting them on the TV. Safety requirements would be important: detect the affected placeholder rather than disabling packages on every TV, preserve the original enabled/disabled state, and restore it on success, cancellation or error. Restarting Couch TV after import would also make the new scenes appear in rotation.

This worked for importing local photos on the TCL above without USB storage or hosting. The current web-address fallback remains useful on TVs where ADB is unavailable.

issues.title: omh update: the package-manager step has no timeout and shows no output while it runs
issues.body:
## Problem

In `omh update`, the command-package step runs the package manager with `subprocess.run(update_command, text=True, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE)` and passes no `timeout` (`src/commands/setup.py:1870-1875`, inside `_run_package_manager_self_update` at `:1853`). The progress header for step 1/2 is printed first (`:1864-1869`). The package manager's output is captured, not streamed, and is shown only if the step fails (`:1876-1882`).

I have not reproduced a hang. This comes from reading the code: if the npm, pip or bun install stalls (network, a lock, or a registry that never answers), `omh update` would wait indefinitely after the step header with no output.

## Complete user goal

When the package-manager step stalls, a person running `omh update` either sees progress or gets a bounded failure. Today they get a silent wait.

## Intended surfaces

Not executor-specific: the `omh update` CLI (installer-managed package-manager path).

## Observed evidence

- `src/commands/setup.py:1870-1875`: `subprocess.run` with `stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE` and no `timeout=`.
- `src/commands/setup.py:1889`: the re-entry `subprocess.run([*reentry_command, *argv], env=env)` also has no timeout, but it inherits the terminal, so its output is visible.
- No hang was observed. This is a code-reading report only.

## Proposal

Two options, separate or combined:

1. Add a timeout to the package-manager call and convert `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` into the existing `OmhError("command package update failed: ...")` path.
2. Stream or tee the package manager's output when the update is not in `--json` mode.

## Alternatives considered

Leave it as it is: package managers have their own network timeouts, and an interrupt with Ctrl-C still works.

## Boundaries and risks

A fixed bound could cut off a legitimately slow first install on a slow link. Streamed output would change the human-readable `omh update` output that tests may pin.

## Decision requested

Do you want a timeout and/or streamed progress for this step? If you want a timeout, what bound?

issues.title: [Bug] SSH TUI 终端：非沉浸模式下 vim / 备用屏程序显示错位（目标 PTY 高度因 TUI 菜单栏少或多了 N 行）
issues.body:
### 产品版本

v5.1.1

### 版本类型

- [x] 社区版
- [ ] 企业版
- [ ] 企业试用版

### 安装方式

- [ ] 在线安装 (一键命令安装)
- [ ] 离线包安装
- [x] All-in-One
- [ ] 1Panel
- [ ] Kubernetes
- [ ] 源码安装

### 环境信息

- JumpServer / KoKo：v5.x（dev 分支；在 commit 895a4f1 上复现）
- 接入路径：ssh user@<jumpserver> -p 2222 → 交互式 TUI → 选择一台 SSH 资产 → 进入交互 shell
- 目标机：任意 Linux 主机；vim（任意较新版本）
- 客户端：macOS Terminal 和 NyaTerm 均复现 → 尺寸偏差发生在服务端 KoKo TUI，与客户端无关

### 🐛 缺陷描述

JumpServer v5 的 SSH 交互式终端（KoKo TUI）中，使用备用屏（alternate screen buffer）的全屏程序 —— vim、htop、less 等 —— 在非沉浸式（带菜单栏/chrome）TUI 模式下会显示错位。 猜测原因是 TUI 为目标会话预留了菜单栏行，导致目标 PTY 被告知比物理终端少几行。 把会话切换到沉浸式模式（快捷键 z）后，PTY 高度等于完整终端高度，vim 即恢复正常。

### 复现步骤

1. 连接：ssh admin@<jumpserver> -p 2222，进入交互式 TUI。
2. 选择一台 SSH 资产，打开交互 shell（非沉浸式，带 TUI 菜单栏）。
3. 运行 vim <file>（需要文件里有超过一屏的内容），把光标移到屏幕底部，例如按 o 新开一行。
4. 观察错位：底部内容错开约既行，和/或 TUI 菜单栏区域与编辑器内容重叠。


### 期望结果

vim htop 等正常铺满整个终端或窗口区域，和直连目标机（绕过 JumpServer）表现一致。

### 补充信息

实测证据（同一个物理窗口）
** 过 JumpServer —— 非沉浸式 TUI **

```bash
$ stty size
32 151
```

** 直连 —— 同一窗口，绕过 JumpServer **

```bash
$ stty size
34 151

$ echo $TERM
xterm-256color
```

stty size 输出为 rows cols。同一个 34 行的窗口；过 JumpServer 时目标 PTY 是 32 行 → 少 2 行。 cols 完全相同。

### 尝试过的解决方案

在 TUI 会话里按c trl+b z 进入沉浸式模式；vim 及其它备用屏程序即正常工作。但是 htop 还是会受到 "ctrl+b:Exit immersive mode" 信息的一次干扰，需要按下键刷过去一页才能恢复。

issues.title: Newly created Thermal Comfort entities are disabled after every Home Assistant restart
issues.body:
Environment
Home Assistant Core: latest stable (2026.6.x)
Thermal Comfort: 2.2.6 (HACS)
Describe the bug

I noticed an issue with newly created Thermal Comfort entities.

After creating new sensors and enabling all entities, everything works as expected.

However, after a full Home Assistant restart, several of these newly created entities become disabled again and have to be enabled manually.

This does not happen when simply reloading the integration from Settings → Devices & Services. It only happens after a complete Home Assistant restart.

Older Thermal Comfort entities that were created months ago are not affected and remain enabled across restarts.

Affected sensor types

The issue affects newly created calculated sensors such as:

Moist Air Enthalpy (moist_air_enthalpy)
Heat Index
Humidex
Summer Simmer Index
Frost Point

Older entities of the same integration continue to work normally.

Steps to reproduce
Create a new Thermal Comfort device.
Enable all newly created entities.
Verify that the sensors are working.
Restart Home Assistant.
The same entities are disabled again.
Expected behavior

Once an entity has been enabled by the user, it should remain enabled after Home Assistant restarts.

Actual behavior

Newly created Thermal Comfort entities become disabled after every Home Assistant restart.

Additional observations
The issue is reproducible on every restart.
Reloading the integration does not reproduce the issue.
Existing older Thermal Comfort entities remain enabled.
Only recently created entities are affected.
I could not find any related errors in the Home Assistant logs.

While investigating the Home Assistant entity registry (core.entity_registry), I noticed that entities from other integrations (e.g. Sun, UniFi, HomematicIP Local) are intentionally registered with "disabled_by": "integration".

For the Thermal Comfort entities I inspected, however, disabled_by was null, which makes me wonder if the entities are recreated or their registry entries are modified during Home Assistant startup.

If additional diagnostics or debug logging would help, I'd be happy to provide them.

issues.title: compile records survive OS profile switches and replay a stale target triple
issues.body:
# Issue — switching OS profile leaves compile records that poison the archive builders

**Target:** `UniXNU/UniXNU`

## Symptom

After building once with one OS profile, building the same device with another
fails in an archive recipe with a target conflict that names a deployment
version nobody asked for:

```
clang: error: overriding '-mios-version-min=27.0' option with
       '--target=arm64e-apple-ios17.0.0' [-Werror,-Woverriding-option]
```

`python3 -c` on the environment shows the correct target
(`arch=arm64e ios=27.0`), so nothing in the build's own environment explains
`ios17.0.0`.

## Cause

`scripts/build-arm-driver.py` *replays* a compile record captured during the
XNU bootstrap pass:

```python
result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=record['directory'], ...)   # build-arm-driver.py:108
```

Records live in `<tree>/build/xnu/**/*.o.json` and survive across profile
switches. The replayed command carries the triple baked in at capture time, so
a tree bootstrapped against iOS 17 keeps compiling iOS 17 objects while the
current profile says 27.0.

`build_archives()` logs *"Revalidate the selected source and regenerate headers
on every archive build"* — the records are revalidated, but their recorded
command line is still the old one.

## Ask

One of:

- key the record cache on the profile (arch + `ios_version` + XNU revision) and
  invalidate when it changes, or
- detect a target mismatch between a record's command and the current
  `kernel_target.TRIPLE` and fail with a message that says "delete
  `<tree>/build/xnu`", instead of letting clang report an `-Werror` conflict.

For now, every profile switch needs

```sh
rm -rf out/<device>/<os_profile>/<config>/tree/build/xnu
```

which is not documented anywhere I could find (`docs/guide/build-kernel.md`
does not mention it).

---

## Provenance

Reported by an AI coding agent (DeepSeek) during a device port; not written up by a human who
verified each sentence. The evidence offered is therefore meant to be run, not believed: every
claim below is a command with a deterministic output, and the versions that produced it are named.

issues.title: Device-repo bootstrap: how is the first build/native-prelink candidate produced?
issues.body:
﻿## Question

A device repository's ordered archive recipes read a **previous build's** output from
`build/native-prelink/`, and `build/` is pruned from git. Is there a documented order in
which those archives can be produced from a clean tree, or is a seed artifact required?

Concretely, with `UniXNU/UniXNU@main` + `ljhhkx529/unixnu-fuxi@old` + `ljhhkx529/uefi-fuxi@old`
(`drivers/QcomXnuUsbDebug` repointed to `xiaoleGun/QcomXnuUsbDebug@e2e2b7c7`), on a
`macos-26` GitHub Actions runner with Xcode 26.6, `./unixnu build kernel` stops in the
archive chain:

```
== kernel: archive-11-build-sheng-platform-power
No reference candidate available
```

The recipes that need it:

| script | file it reads |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/build-sheng-platform-power.py:91` | `native-owner-ufs-rootauth3-candidate.macho` (fallback glob `native-owner-ufs-cpu-desktop-*-candidate.macho`) |
| `scripts/build-native-legacy-display.py:111` | `native-owner-mobile-graphics-candidate.macho` (same fallback) |
| `scripts/build-native-aes-bindings.py:62` | `native-defaults-candidate.macho` + `native-defaults-candidate.json` |
| `scripts/build-native-hid-input.py:17` | `native-owner-ufs-cpu-desktop-v9-hid-init-candidate.macho` |

There is no binary larger than 200 KB in any branch of that repository, and no release
asset, so a clean checkout has nothing to point at.

## What I tried

The escape hatch documented in that repo's `scripts/build-legacy-stub.py` (Stage A: link a
kernel without the storage and display stacks, then prelink it). That works:

```
Experimental candidate: 51818496 bytes; executable bytes unchanged; runtime unqualified
```

but the result cannot act as the reference. `build-native-legacy-display.py:105` needs the
candidate to carry relocations for the 358-entry `IOMobileFramebufferLegacy` vtable:

```python
compiled = [relocations.get(vtable + 16 + i * 8) for i in range(358)]
require(all(compiled) and vtable + 16 + 358 * 8 not in relocations, 'Exact owned 358-entry vtable')
```

In the Stage A candidate, `IOMobileFramebufferLegacy` and `ApplePMGR` appear only inside the
`__PRELINK_INFO`/kext text — never in a symbol table and never as relocations — so
`all(compiled)` is false. Generation 0 therefore looks underivable from public sources.

## Ask

1. Is the intended bootstrap order documented anywhere (which recipe produced the first
   candidate, and what was stubbed or disabled to link it)?
2. Or is a seed `native-owner-ufs-cpu-desktop-*-candidate.macho` deliberately required, in
   which case what is the minimal contract it has to satisfy?

Reproduction (my fork, public): Stage A run 42366075469 produces the prelink candidate
(https://github.com/chipppppppps/fuxi-t50/actions/runs/42366075469), and the full workflow
stops at archive-11 as above (https://github.com/chipppppppps/fuxi-t50/actions/runs/42365883116).

Note: `ljhhkx529/unixnu-fuxi` has issues disabled, so I am asking here where the build
system is maintained. Happy to move this elsewhere if that is the preference.

issues.title: Spec shows as just started and cannot be opened or removed after its worktree is removed or branch changes
issues.body:
## Summary
When a spec is created and its worktree is later removed, or the worktree's branch changes, the spec shows up in the UI as if it had just started. Opening it fails with "Not Found", and the spec cannot be removed.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a spec. It gets a git worktree and branch.
2. Remove the worktree (`git worktree remove`), or change the branch checked out in it.
3. Open the specs list in the dashboard.
4. Click the spec.

## Actual behavior
- The spec is listed as if it were just started (progress/state appears reset).
- Clicking it shows a "Not Found" error.
- Delete/remove on the spec does not work, so it is stuck in the list.

## Expected behavior
- The spec's state should not depend on the worktree still existing on the expected branch. If the worktree or branch is gone, show a clear "worktree missing" or "branch changed" state.
- The spec should always be removable, even when its worktree is missing.
- Ideally offer to recreate or re-attach the worktree.

## Environment
- Kiro Crew 0.12.1 (source checkout)
- Linux, dashboard UI

## Notes
Likely cause (not verified): spec state is resolved through the worktree path or branch, so a missing worktree makes lookup return 404 in both the detail and delete paths.
