issues.title: [yaxuanm/qdrant] Hybrid Search fails on named-vector collections (dense/sparse)
issues.body:
## Plugin
yaxuanm/qdrant v0.0.1

## Problem
Hybrid Search fails on collections with named vectors (`dense`, `sparse`) created outside the plugin (e.g. custom embed scripts).
**Error:** Qdrant responded with HTTP 400: Wrong input: Not existing vector name error:


## Root cause
1. Operation inference checks `text` before hybrid indicators → runs `operation: "query"` instead of `hybrid_search`
2. Plain query sends unnamed `vector` to `/points/search` — invalid when collection has only named vectors
3. Sparse vector is not generated from `text` in hybrid path (only dense embedding is created)
## Reproduction
- Collection: named vectors `dense` (3072) + `sparse`
- Tool: Qdrant · Hybrid Search
- Inputs: `text`, `using_dense: dense`, `using_sparse: sparse`, `fusion_method: rrf`
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-large
## Expected
`hybrid_search` → `/points/query` with prefetch using `dense` and `sparse`
## Actual
`query` → `/points/search` with flat `vector` array (no vector name)
## Fix verified locally (v0.0.2)
- Route hybrid before text→query
- Set `operation: hybrid_search` on hybrid tool YAML
- Generate sparse via `fastembed` (`Qdrant/bm25`)
- Add `fastembed` dependency
## Environment
- Dify 1.14.2 (self-hosted)
- Qdrant Cloud
- Plugin: yaxuanm/qdrant 0.0.1 from Marketplace

issues.title: Plugin request: Hive — social media management (OpenAPI 3.1 + remote MCP)
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

Hive

### Function Description

Social media management inside a Dify workflow: publish and schedule across twelve networks, read cross-account analytics, work a shared inbox, and build DM automations for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok.

Scenarios people would build:
- An agent drafts a post, validates it against each network's rules, and schedules it
- A scheduled workflow pulls last week's numbers across every connected account and writes a summary
- A form submission becomes an idea on the content board

Everything needed to build the plugin is already published:

- **OpenAPI 3.1**: https://hivepublish.com/api/v1/openapi.json — 50 endpoints, one per tool, each with an operationId, responses and a description
- **Auth**: bearer token — a scoped API key from Hive (Settings → API) or an OAuth 2.1 access token
- **Remote MCP server**: https://hivepublish.com/api/mcp (OAuth 2.1 + dynamic client registration), listed on the official MCP Registry as `com.hivepublish/hive`
- **Docs**: https://hivepublish.com/developers

Good first tools: `create_draft`, `schedule_post`, `read_analytics_summary`, `read_posts`, `read_calendar`, `search`, `fetch`.

One behaviour worth modelling: anything that would reach a real audience — scheduling, public replies, direct messages, setting an automation live — does not execute on the API call. It returns a single-use approval URL that the account holder confirms inside Hive, and the call is re-sent with that token. Reads and draft creation run immediately. A plugin should surface the approval URL as output rather than treat it as an error.

### Official Website URL

https://hivepublish.com — docs at https://hivepublish.com/developers

issues.title: TCL Android 14: Home reverts to Google TV after every reboot (+ suggested fix)
issues.body:
## Summary

On a TCL Google TV running Android 14, couch-tv works perfectly until the TV reboots. After every reboot the Home button goes back to Google TV and cannot be recovered from the TV itself, because TCL's own boot manager (`TclAppBoot`) blocks three things:

1. binding `FireWatch`
2. binding `KeyWatch`
3. delivering `BOOT_COMPLETED` to `FireWatch$Restore`

The stated reason in the log is that the app does not hold TCL's `AUTO_START` app-op. Setting that app-op over adb works, but **TCL resets it to `ignore` on every boot**, so it never helps at the moment it is needed.

This is a different cause from #51 (which is about `VanillaModeHomeActivity` not matching `isStockHome()`). Here the activity class is the normal `launcherx/.home.HomeActivity`; the services are simply never bound.

## Device

```
model        TCL Smart TV Pro (G08_4K_GB)
fingerprint  TCL/G08_4K_GB/G08:14/UTT2.250416.001/AU02:user/release-keys
Android      14 (SDK 34)
patch level  2025-12-05
ABI          armeabi-v7a
couch-tv     0.12, option A (no bridge)
```

Installed with `adb install`, home set with `cmd package set-home-activity app.couchtv.launcher/.MainActivity`, services enabled by writing `enabled_accessibility_services` and `accessibility_enabled`.

## What works

Immediately after setup, everything behaves as documented:

- Home from inside an app goes to couch-tv
- Back from inside an app lands on couch-tv
- Forcing the stock home with `am start -n com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx/.home.HomeActivity` is taken over by FireWatch in **under 1 second**
- `dumpsys accessibility` shows both services bound: `label=Home button watch` and `label=Home gear button`

## What breaks

After `adb reboot` (and after a real power cut):

```
accessibility_enabled  = 0
Bound services         = {}
foreground             = com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx/.home.HomeActivity
```

`enabled_accessibility_services` still lists both services, and both are listed under `Enabled services` in `dumpsys accessibility`, but `Bound services` is empty. Writing `accessibility_enabled 1` again over adb does **not** rebind them, and nothing is logged by `AccessibilityManagerService` when it is written.

The services also never appear in the TV's own Settings → Accessibility menu, so there is no way to switch them back on with the remote. The menu only lists Switch Access.

## The actual cause

`logcat` right after boot:

```
D AccessibilityManagerService: Ignoring non-encryption-aware service ComponentInfo{app.couchtv.launcher/app.couchtv.launcher.FireWatch}
D AccessibilityManagerService: Ignoring non-encryption-aware service ComponentInfo{app.couchtv.launcher/app.couchtv.launcher.KeyWatch}

I TclAppBoot: TclAppBootInfo{callerPkgName = 'android', calleePkgName = 'app.couchtv.launcher',
  calleeComponent = 'app.couchtv.launcher/.FireWatch', bootType = 'bind_service',
  isAutoStart = 'true', isAllow = 'false',
  reason = 'callee_doesn't_have_OP_AUTO_START_permission.', count = '1'}
W ActivityManager: [TclAppBoot]:forbid bind service ComponentInfo{app.couchtv.launcher/app.couchtv.launcher.FireWatch}
W ActivityManager: [TclAppBoot]:forbid bind service ComponentInfo{app.couchtv.launcher/app.couchtv.launcher.KeyWatch}

I TclAppBoot: TclAppBootInfo{callerPkgName = 'android', calleePkgName = 'app.couchtv.launcher',
  calleeComponent = 'app.couchtv.launcher/.FireWatch$Restore', bootType = 'broadcast',
  broadcastAction = 'android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED',
  isAutoStart = 'true', isAllow = 'false',
  reason = 'callee_doesn't_have_OP_AUTO_START_permission.', count = '1'}
```

So couch-tv's own repair path (`FireWatch$Restore` on `BOOT_COMPLETED`) is correct and would fix this by itself — TCL never lets it run.

## Why granting the app-op does not help

The app-op exists and can be set:

```
$ adb shell appops get app.couchtv.launcher AUTO_START
AUTO_START: ignore

$ adb shell appops set app.couchtv.launcher AUTO_START allow
$ adb shell appops get app.couchtv.launcher AUTO_START
AUTO_START: allow
```

But after `adb reboot`:

```
$ adb shell appops get app.couchtv.launcher AUTO_START
AUTO_START: ignore
```

TCL rewrites it every boot for packages that are not on its own whitelist. `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` was granted to couch-tv (`granted=true`) before this test, so the permission is not the limiting factor — the process is simply never started.

## Things ruled out

- `ACCESS_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS` is already `allow`, so Android 13+ restricted settings is not the blocker.
- The HOME role survives the reboot (`cmd role get-role-holders android.app.role.HOME` still returns `app.couchtv.launcher`). Only the services are gone.
- The home activity is the ordinary `.home.HomeActivity`, not `VanillaModeHomeActivity`, so this is not #51.
- Launching the app first and then rewriting the settings does not rebind either.

## Suggested fix

The Haven launcher hit the same TCL boot manager and worked around it by **declaring an empty TV input service** — a `TvInputService` that never surfaces as a selectable input. TCL's whitelist always allows apps that provide a TV input, so the app is allowed to auto-start and its services are allowed to bind.

Its author describes it as:

> TCL's boot manager stopped any app not on its whitelist from starting. It always lets apps that provide a TV input through, so Haven declares an empty TV input service (one that never shows up as an input), and now it comes up by itself after a cold boot.

If couch-tv declared the same kind of placeholder `TvInputService`, `TclAppBoot` should stop blocking `FireWatch`, `KeyWatch` and `FireWatch$Restore`, and the existing restore logic would then work on TCL without any user action.

## Separate, smaller observation

A **real** double-press of Home on the TCL remote lands on `launcherx/.home.HomeActivity` and stays there indefinitely (measured 25s, no recovery). FireWatch does not fire. The same activity started with `am start -n` is taken over in under a second.

So TCL's double-press handler appears to bring the stock launcher forward without producing the `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` event FireWatch listens for. Injected key events (`input keyevent KEYCODE_HOME` twice) do not reproduce it — TCL's handler sits below the layer adb can inject into, so this can only be reproduced with the physical remote. Pressing Back twice is a working escape.

## Workaround in the meantime

A small script run from a computer after each reboot restores it in about ten seconds: set the home activity, start the app once, set `AUTO_START allow`, then write `enabled_accessibility_services` and `accessibility_enabled 1`. That binds both services again until the next reboot.****

issues.title: Running the suite under pytest fails a CLI update test: pytest's bytecode for plugin module test_expectation_check is rejected as unmanaged
issues.body:
## Summary

`pyproject.toml` configures pytest, but one CLI test fails under pytest and passes under unittest. The plugin bundle ships a production module whose name matches pytest's `test_*.py` pattern. When pytest imports that module it writes a pytest-tagged `.pyc` into the installed plugin directory, and the plugin refresh then reports that file as an unmanaged entry.

All references are at 3e3f4c19e.

## Complete user goal

A contributor who runs the dev-group test runner (`uv run --group dev pytest`) gets the same result as the unittest runner that CI and `CLAUDE.md` use.

## Reproduction

At 3e3f4c19e, on macOS with Python 3.14.7 (`uv run python -V`), after `uv sync --group dev`:

1. `uv run --group dev pytest -q "tests/test_cli.py::CliTests::test_direct_update_source_ref_metadata_does_not_claim_command_package_update"`. This fails with `1 failed in 6.81s`.
2. `PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_cli.CliTests.test_direct_update_source_ref_metadata_does_not_claim_command_package_update`. This passes with `Ran 1 test in 10.705s` / `OK`.

## Expected behavior

The test gives the same result under both runners, or the repository stops offering pytest as a runner.

## Affected surfaces

Not executor-specific (contributor test tooling, plus the plugin refresh in `omh update`).

## Observed evidence

- pytest is configured in two places: `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` at `pyproject.toml:35-36` and the dev dependency group at `pyproject.toml:152-154` (`"pytest==9.2.0"`). CI runs unittest through `tools/test_sharding/run.py` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:128-129`, `:288-289`). `CLAUDE.md:86-87` documents `python -m unittest`.
- `src/plugin_bundle/omh/test_expectation_check.py` is production code: the hooks import it at `src/plugin_bundle/omh/hooks/llm_hooks.py:61` and `src/plugin_bundle/omh/hooks/verify_hooks.py:20`. Its name matches pytest's default `test_*.py` pattern, so pytest's assertion rewriting writes `__pycache__/test_expectation_check.cpython-314-pytest-9.2.0.pyc` next to the installed copy.
- `_generated_plugin_bytecode` (`src/install/plugin_pack.py:574-581`) accepts a `__pycache__` file only if `importlib.util.source_from_cache` maps it back to a managed source, and it returns `False` on `ValueError`. With the pytest tag in the name, `source_from_cache` raises `ValueError: expected only 2 or 3 dots in 'test_expectation_check.cpython-314-pytest-9.2.0.pyc'`. The plain `test_expectation_check.cpython-314.pyc` maps back to `test_expectation_check.py`. I checked both names with a short Python call. The rejected file is then listed as unknown (`src/install/plugin_pack.py:564-565`).
- The failing assertion is `tests/test_cli.py:13977`.

## Acceptance criteria

The maintainers decide which runner the repository supports, and the chosen runner passes this test.

## Environment

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Python 3.14.7 (uv default), pytest 9.2.0 (dev group), revision 3e3f4c19e.

## Logs or output

```text
>           self.assertEqual(status, 0, stderr)
E           AssertionError: 1 != 0 : note: OMH plugin refresh skipped: unmanaged plugin entries: __pycache__/test_expectation_check.cpython-314-pytest-9.2.0.pyc; plugin directory left unchanged; move these entries outside the plugin directory, or use --force to replace them. Inspect <tmp>/.hermes/plugins/omh before choosing `omh setup --force`.

tests/test_cli.py:13977: AssertionError
FAILED tests/test_cli.py::CliTests::test_direct_update_source_ref_metadata_does_not_claim_command_package_update
1 failed in 6.81s
```

## Decision requested

Should pytest be a supported runner? If so, there are two possible fixes: rename the module so it no longer matches `test_*.py`, or have `_generated_plugin_bytecode` accept pytest-tagged caches of managed sources. If not, the `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` table and the `pytest` dev group could be dropped. I can send a PR for whichever option you prefer.

issues.title: CI does not run the test suite on macOS or inside a Hermes session environment
issues.body:
## Problem

The full unittest suite runs in CI on ubuntu (Python 3.11 on pull requests, plus 3.13 on pushes) and on windows (3.12): `.github/workflows/ci.yml:84-95` and `:251-263`. macOS gets only the `distribution` job, which builds and installs the package but does not run the suite (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:556-560`). Every lane starts from a clean runner environment, so no CI lane runs the suite inside a Hermes session shell.

I ran the full suite locally at 3e3f4c19e on macOS, from a shell started inside a Hermes session. Eight tests failed. None of the failures is shown to be specific to macOS or to Python 3.14. Seven of them come from the Hermes session environment leaking into the tests, which CI cannot see because CI never runs inside such a session. I am not reporting an OS bug. My question is whether CI should cover these two environments.

## Complete user goal

Contributors who run the suite on macOS, or from a Hermes or OMH TUI session (a common setup for people working on OMH), get the same result as CI.

## Intended surfaces

Not executor-specific (test suite and CI).

## Observed evidence

Environment: macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), `uv run python` reported Python 3.14.7, detached worktree at 3e3f4c19e. The shell was inside a Hermes/OMH TUI session, so `HERMES_TUI_DIR`, `HERMES_CRON_SESSION`, `HERMES_PYTHON` and other session variables were set. I planned the run with `tools/test_sharding/plan.py --shards 4` (25,648 tests discovered, 77 quarantined) and ran four shards with `tools/test_sharding/run.py --lane local --workers 2`, followed by the quarantine set.

Result: 25,483 tests executed in the shards, with 6 failures and 2 errors. The 77 quarantined tests passed.

1. Four `test_omh_resume_door` tests fail with `'HERMES_TUI_DIR' unexpectedly found in {...}`, because `HERMES_TUI_DIR` is inherited from the session: `FallbackTargetTests.test_no_node_opens_plain_hermes`, `FallbackTargetTests.test_no_termios_with_node_opens_hermes_own_tui`, `FallbackTargetTests.test_the_fallback_code_with_node_opens_hermes_own_tui` and `OmhTuiDoorTests.test_without_the_omh_tui_and_without_node_plain_hermes_runs`. #2789 fixes this leak.
2. Three more tests depend on the session environment:
   - `test_repeat_call_breaker.UnattendedLaneTest.test_cron_is_not_detectable_from_a_plugin_and_reads_as_attended` fails with `AssertionError: '' is not None` at `self.assertIsNone(os.environ.get("HERMES_CRON_SESSION"))` (`tests/test_repeat_call_breaker.py:1416`). The session exports `HERMES_CRON_SESSION=''`.
   - `test_plugin_distribution.PluginHermesAdmissionTests.test_real_admission_accepts_declared_range` (`tests/test_plugin_distribution.py:393`) fails with `observed False ... loader_probe_failed ... ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'`.
   - `test_plugin_distribution.PluginHermesAdmissionTests.test_real_admission_rejects_unsupported_version_before_register` (`tests/test_plugin_distribution.py:359-364`) errors with `CalledProcessError` from `<~/.hermes/tools/python-3.14.x>/bin/python3 -c 'from hermes_cli import __version__'`.

     Both of these tests take `HERMES_PYTHON` before anything else when they choose an interpreter: the first through `_loader_command` (`src/install/plugin_loader_observation.py:185-189`), the second through `_find_hermes_python` (`src/install/plugin_loader_observation.py:256-259`). The session set `HERMES_PYTHON` to a Hermes-managed tools `python3` that does not have `hermes_cli` installed.
3. `test_ai_job_search_state.JobStateTests.test_aggregate_proposed_state_size_preserves_bytes` (`tests/test_ai_job_search_state.py:762`) errors with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. The error comes from the 15 s timeout in the `cli` helper (`tests/test_ai_job_search_state.py:112-113`), reached through the `merge(value, exit=2)` call at `:786`. I saw this with eight workers running at once (four shards × `--workers 2`), so it looks load-sensitive. I did not re-run it on its own.

Nothing above shows a macOS-specific or 3.14-specific difference. CI cannot observe items 1 and 2 because no lane runs inside a Hermes session environment.

## Proposal

Options, separate or combined:

- Add a macOS lane, possibly push-only like the 3.13 lane, and/or the newest Python, to the test matrix.
- Make the suite's base test environment clear the Hermes session variables (`HERMES_TUI_DIR`, `HERMES_CRON_SESSION`, `HERMES_PYTHON`, ...) so that local runs are hermetic. A CI lane that sets a few of them would then catch regressions.

## Alternatives considered

Keep the matrix as it is and document that the suite should be run from a clean shell rather than from inside a Hermes session.

## Boundaries and risks

macOS runners cost more and are slower. The `aggregate` job's `EXPECTED_LANES` pin (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:92-94`) would need to change with any new lane.

## Decision requested

Should macOS and/or the newest Python be added to the test matrix? Separately, should the tests be hermetic against an ambient Hermes session environment?

issues.title: [Bug] 会话时间随 PATCH 更新累积 +8h 偏移，导致录像路径错位
issues.body:
## 产品版本

v5.1.1-ce

补充：v4.10.19-ce 产生的历史会话也存在相同偏移。升级前后的数据库 dump 对比确认，v5 迁移没有改写这些旧值，因此不是本次 v5 迁移引入的数据变更。

## 版本类型

- [x] 社区版
- [ ] 企业版
- [ ] 企业试用版

## 安装方式

自维护 Docker Compose，使用官方镜像：

- `jumpserver/core:v5.1.1-ce`
- `jumpserver/koko:v5.1.1-ce`
- `jumpserver/chen:v5.1.1-ce`
- `jumpserver/web:v5.1.1-ce`
- `jumpserver/kael:v5.1.1-ce`

## 环境信息

- 宿主：Debian 13，内核 6.12
- Docker：29.7.2
- core：Python 3.14.8、Django 5.2.17
- PostgreSQL 18.6，经 pgbouncer 1.25.2 访问，`pool_mode=transaction`
- Redis 8.4.0
- koko 容器时间正确，`TZ=Asia/Shanghai`
- core：`TIME_ZONE='Asia/Shanghai'`、`USE_TZ=True`
- 直连 PG 时 `SHOW timezone` 为 `Asia/Shanghai`；Django 连接和实际 PG 参数均为 `UTC`

## 缺陷描述

Web SSH 会话中，koko 发给 core 的 UTC 时间正确，但 core 在后续会话 PATCH 中会重写未随请求变更的时间字段，并出现每次 8 小时的累积偏移。

以实际开始时间为 `2026-11-10 17:15:05 +08:00` 的会话为例，两次更新后：

- `date_start` 变为 `2026-11-11 09:15:05 +08:00`，偏移 +16 小时；
- `date_end` 变为 `2026-11-11 01:15:12 +08:00`，偏移 +8 小时。

从 SQL 参数看，已有时间的本地表观值被保留下来，同时时区标签被改成 UTC。例如本地 `17:15:05 +08:00` 被写成 `17:15:05 +00:00`，两者已不再是同一时刻。

## 影响范围

1. 会话列表、审计记录中的开始/结束时间与真实操作时间不一致，时长也可能随之失真。
2. core 按 `session.date_start.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')` 生成录像路径，而实际 `.cast.gz` 文件位于真实会话日期目录。日期漂移后页面提示录像文件不存在，但文件实际仍在磁盘上，asciicast 文件头和内容完好。
3. chen 的 Web 数据库会话也观察到相同的 `date_start` 偏移，因此问题可能不局限于 koko。本文的 HTTP/SQL 抓包样本来自 koko Web SSH。

## 复现步骤

1. 普通用户通过 Web 终端打开一条 SSH 会话。
2. 执行一条命令并关闭会话。
3. 等待录像上传完成。
4. 分别在创建、后续每次 PATCH 后查询 `terminal_session.date_start` 和 `date_end`。
5. 对照 koko 的 HTTP 请求、core 响应和 core 发往 PG 的 UPDATE 参数。

## 期望结果

- 会话时间等于真实开始、结束时间。
- PATCH 未携带时间字段时，不应改变数据库中的既有时间。
- 历史录像能继续命中磁盘上的 `.cast.gz` 文件。

## 实际结果与证据

### 多次复现

同一天多条 Web SSH 测试会话均出现相同的最终偏移，不是单条脏数据：

| 会话 ID | 实际开始时间（+08） | 最终 date_start（+08） | 最终 date_end（+08） |
|---|---|---|---|
| `97c23c46-5663-4c44-a0e7-47e1337801ee` | 2026-11-10 16:56:00 | 2026-11-11 08:56:00（+16h） | 2026-11-11 00:56:27（+8h） |
| `b5271f79-c628-41b3-805e-e4a6d423c43d` | 2026-11-10 17:01:55 | 2026-11-11 09:01:55（+16h） | 2026-11-11 01:02:05（+8h） |
| `bd3f429b-e1f8-4d96-873e-66d849b34093` | 2026-11-10 17:15:05 | 2026-11-11 09:15:05（+16h） | 2026-11-11 01:15:12（+8h） |

以下 HTTP/SQL 证据来自最后一条会话。认证头、token、资产凭据和终端内容均已去除。

### 1. koko 创建会话时发送的 UTC 时间正确

```text
POST /api/v1/terminal/sessions/
koko -> core: "date_start":"2026-11-10 09:15:05 +0000"

core 创建响应:
"date_start":"2026/11/10 17:15:05 +0800"
```

实际本地开始时间为 `2026-11-10 17:15:05 +08:00`，上述两个值表示同一时刻，均正确。

### 2. 第一次更新后，date_start 增加 8 小时

koko 发送的结束时间仍正确：

```text
PATCH /api/v1/terminal/sessions/<session-id>/
"date_end":"2026-11-10 09:15:12 +0000"
```

core 随后经 pgbouncer 向 PG 发出：

```sql
"date_start" = '2026-11-10T17:15:05+00:00'
"date_end"   = '2026-11-10T17:15:12+08:00'
```

这里 `date_start` 的表观值是本地时间 `17:15:05`，但时区被标成了 UTC。对应响应变为：

```text
"date_start":"2026/11/11 01:15:05 +0800"
"date_end":"2026/11/10 17:15:12 +0800"
```

### 3. 第二次更新后，两个字段再各增加 8 小时

```sql
"date_start" = '2026-11-11T01:15:05+00:00'
"date_end"   = '2026-11-10T17:15:12+00:00'
```

最终数据库值（Asia/Shanghai 显示）：

```text
date_start = 2026-11-11 09:15:05+08
date_end   = 2026-11-11 01:15:12+08
```

## 已做的排除与验证

- koko 容器时钟和时区配置正常。
- 运行中的 koko 二进制包含预期依赖 `v0.0.0-20260826024103-e9e4992f746b`。
- SDK 明确调用 `time.Now().UTC()`，JSON 中带数值型 UTC 偏移。
- core DRF 能正确解析 koko 的 `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS +0000` 格式。
- Django 时间适配器保留 aware UTC，psycopg 输出 `+00:00::timestamptz`。
- `terminal_session` 上没有自定义触发器或规则。
- 在 shell 中直接执行 `Session.save()`、`SessionSerializer.save()` 以及直接调用 `SessionViewSet.partial_update` 均未单独复现偏移；上述证据来自真实 HTTP 请求链路。因此目前能确定偏移发生在真实 HTTP 运行链路，但尚未定位到具体代码行。

## 相关源码位置

- koko 通过 `common.NewNowUTCTime()` 设置会话开始时间：
  https://github.com/jumpserver/koko/blob/v5.1.1/pkg/proxy/server.go#L115-L118
- SDK 的 UTC 构造函数与 JSON 序列化：
  https://github.com/jumpserver-dev/sdk-go/blob/e9e4992f746b/common/time.go#L11-L26
- core 按 `date_start` 生成录像路径：
  https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/blob/v5.1.1/apps/terminal/models/session/session.py#L82-L93
- core 会话序列化器更新逻辑：
  https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/blob/v5.1.1/apps/terminal/serializers/session.py#L168-L187
- core SessionViewSet 查询与更新路径：
  https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/blob/v5.1.1/apps/terminal/api/session/session.py#L226-L239
- DRF 时间显示与输入格式：
  https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/blob/v5.1.1/apps/jumpserver/settings/libs.py#L56-L62

## 希望官方协助确认

1. 真实 HTTP PATCH 链路中是否有代码把已带时区的时间先转成本地表观值，再标记为 UTC。
2. 部分更新是否可以不重写未变化的时间字段，例如按实际变更字段限制 ORM 写入范围。
3. 对已漂移的历史数据，官方是否有推荐的修复方式。目前真实开始时刻仍可从 asciicast `.cast.gz` 文件头的 Unix `timestamp` 恢复。

## 关联 issue

https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/issues/16932 也有录像缺失现象，但没有本次这种逐次 PATCH 累积偏移的证据。

issues.title: Kernel layout puts each class's MetaClass vtable immediately after its class vtable, so slot 171 of the class vtable lands on the MetaClass vtable's first entry
issues.body:
### Summary

In kernels produced by this tree, **170 of 176** classes have `__ZTV<Class>` immediately followed by their own `__ZTV<Class>::MetaClass` in `(__DATA_CONST,__const)`. Apple's stock 21H461 kernelcache does this for 75 of 135.

**19 classes** have the two tables exactly `0x558` apart, which is the class vtable's own total span. Reading the vtable at index 171 on any of them therefore lands on the **MetaClass vtable's first entry**, which is `<Class>::MetaClassD1Ev` — the MetaClass complete-object destructor. All 19 were checked individually; 19/19 resolve to `~OSMetaClass` (`0xfffffff00be69368`).

One of the 19 — `IOService` — is connected to an observed crash on an SM8250 device port. The other 18 have the same verified table structure, but no runtime evidence that a dispatch ever reached them.

### Affected classes

Counting only `__ZTV*` symbols in the main kernel's `(__DATA_CONST,__const)`, paired by symbol name (`__ZTV<cls>` ↔ `__ZTVN<cls>9MetaClassE`, not by adjacency):

```
ZTV symbols total            : 346
  plain __ZTV<Class>         : 176   (all in __DATA_CONST,__const)
  __ZTVN<C>9MetaClassE       : 170
duplicate ZTV symbol names   : 0
unexpected naming forms      : 0
```

170 of the 176 plain vtables have a matching MetaClass vtable and are immediately followed by it. The remaining 6 have no `__ZTVN<cls>9MetaClassE` counterpart: `OSMetaClassBase`, `OSMetaClass`, `OSMetaClassMeta` (the metaclass machinery itself) and `IONVRAMCHRPHandler`, `IONVRAMV3Handler`, `IODTNVRAMFormatHandler`. 19 of the 170 pairs are exactly `0x558` apart:

| class | `__ZTV` | `__ZTVN<cls>9MetaClassE` | slot 0 target | symbol at that address |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IOService` | `0xfffffff0071b9a30` | `0xfffffff0071b9f88` | `0xfffffff00bee0c38` | `__ZN9IOService9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOResources` | `0xfffffff0071ba648` | `0xfffffff0071baba0` | `0xfffffff00bee0c68` | `__ZN11IOResources9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOUserResources` | `0xfffffff0071bac38` | `0xfffffff0071bb190` | `0xfffffff00bee0c70` | `__ZN15IOUserResources9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOExclaveProxy` | `0xfffffff0071bb228` | `0xfffffff0071bb780` | `0xfffffff00bee0c78` | `__ZN14IOExclaveProxy9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `_IOServiceStateNotification` | `0xfffffff0071bb958` | `0xfffffff0071bbeb0` | `0xfffffff00bee0c88` | `__ZN27_IOServiceStateNotification9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOServiceCompatibility` | `0xfffffff0071bc088` | `0xfffffff0071bc5e0` | `0xfffffff00bee0c98` | `__ZN22IOServiceCompatibility9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOPlatformDevice` | `0xfffffff0071c2e08` | `0xfffffff0071c3360` | `0xfffffff00bf1af94` | `__ZN16IOPlatformDevice9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IODTNVRAMPlatformNotifier` | `0xfffffff0071c5478` | `0xfffffff0071c59d0` | `0xfffffff00bf28b2c` | `__ZN25IODTNVRAMPlatformNotifier9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IODTNVRAMDiags` | `0xfffffff0071c5a68` | `0xfffffff0071c5fc0` | `0xfffffff00bf28b34` | `__ZN14IODTNVRAMDiags9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IODTNVRAMVariables` | `0xfffffff0071c6058` | `0xfffffff0071c65b0` | `0xfffffff00bf28b3c` | `__ZN18IODTNVRAMVariables9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `TestIOConnectMapMemoryPortLeak45265408` | `0xfffffff0071cb878` | `0xfffffff0071cbdd0` | `0xfffffff00bf436c4` | `__ZN38TestIOConnectMapMemoryPortLeak452654089MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `TestIOUserClient2022Entitlements` | `0xfffffff0071cc4e8` | `0xfffffff0071cca40` | `0xfffffff00bf43cd4` | `__ZN32TestIOUserClient2022Entitlements9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `TestIOServiceUserNotification` | `0xfffffff0071cd1b0` | `0xfffffff0071cd708` | `0xfffffff00bf44238` | `__ZN29TestIOServiceUserNotification9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOUserService` | `0xfffffff0071cee90` | `0xfffffff0071cf3e8` | `0xfffffff00bf5e5dc` | `__ZN13IOUserService9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOSystemStateNotification` | `0xfffffff0071f8b18` | `0xfffffff0071f9070` | `0xfffffff00bf5e60c` | `__ZN25IOSystemStateNotification9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IOPowerConnection` | `0xfffffff0071f9d10` | `0xfffffff0071fa268` | `0xfffffff00bf628d8` | `__ZN17IOPowerConnection9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `IORootParent` | `0xfffffff0071fd380` | `0xfffffff0071fd8d8` | `0xfffffff00bf8276c` | `__ZN12IORootParent9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `NativeUfs` | `0xfffffff007203aa8` | `0xfffffff007204000` | `0xfffffff00bfb25c0` | `__ZN9NativeUfs9MetaClassD1Ev` |
| `NativeUfsBlock` | `0xfffffff007204098` | `0xfffffff0072045f0` | `0xfffffff00bfb25c8` | `__ZN14NativeUfsBlock9MetaClassD1Ev` |

For all 19 the `0x558` delta holds exactly (`__ZTV + 0x558 == __ZTVN<cls>9MetaClassE`), the word at slot 0 is one of the addresses in the fourth column, and that address carries the exact `::MetaClassD1Ev` symbol. Each D1 body is a single 4-byte branch; decoding it and comparing the target against `0xfffffff00be69368` gives 19/19 equal.

Scope, same basis on both sides:

| | Apple stock | this build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain `__ZTV` | 135 | 176 |
| immediately followed by own `::MetaClass` | 75 (56%) | **170 (97%)** |
| of those, gap exactly `0x558` | 3 | **19** |

---

### Crash

Observed on an SM8250 device port (`elish`), `cpus=1`:

```
Kernel data abort                                        [O]  panic report
pc  = 0xfffffff00be6938c      ~OSMetaClass + 0x24        [O] / [D] offset
lr  = 0xfffffff00497dab8      IOStorageFamily.__TEXT_EXEC + 0x11ab8   [O] / [D]
x0  = heap address (differs per run)                     [O]
far = 0x3000c                 identical across every run [O]
esr = 0x96000005              Data abort, same EL, DFSC = translation fault level 1   [O] / [D] decode
```

`lr` is inside the prelinked `com.apple.iokit.IOStorageFamily` kext: `_PrelinkExecutableLoadAddr = 0xfffffff004283580` **[O]** from the `__PRELINK_INFO` plist, and that kext's own Mach-O header declares `__TEXT_EXEC` at `0xfffffff00496c000`, size `0x14358` **[O]**, so `lr` is at `+0x11ab8` **[D]**.

The containing function starts at `0xfffffff00497da34`:

```
0xfffffff00497da34: sub  sp, sp, #128
0xfffffff00497da50: mov  x19, x5
0xfffffff00497da54: mov  x20, x4
0xfffffff00497da58: mov  x21, x3
0xfffffff00497da5c: mov  x22, x2
0xfffffff00497da60: mov  x23, x1
0xfffffff00497da64: mov  x24, x0          ; x24 = incoming x0
...
0xfffffff00497da94: ldr  x8, [x24]        ; x8 = this->vptr
0xfffffff00497da98: ldr  x8, [x8, #1368]  ; x8 = vtable[171]
0xfffffff00497daa0: mov  x0, x24          ; this restored for the call
0xfffffff00497dab4: blr  x8               ; lr = 0xfffffff00497dab8
```

Faulting site, `__ZN11OSMetaClassD2Ev` at `0xfffffff00be69368`:

```
+0x18  mov  x19, x0            ; x19 = this
+0x1c  str  x8, [x0]           ; overwrite vptr — does not fault, so x0 is writable
+0x20  ldr  x8, [x0, #8]       ; x8 = the 8 bytes at object + 8
+0x24  ldr  x20, [x8, #8]      ; fault
```

`far` derivation — `0x00030004` is computed, not observed:

1. `far = 0x3000c` **[O]**;
2. fault instruction is `ldr x20, [x8, #8]` **[O]**, so `far = x8 + 8` **[D]** → `x8 = 0x30004` **[D]**;
3. `x8 = [x0 + 8]` **[O]**, so the 8 bytes at `object + 8` read as `0x0000000000030004` **[D]**;
4. source: `retainCount` is `mutable int` at `OSObject.h:187`, and `OSMetaClassBase` has no data members, so `+8` is `retainCount` and `+0x0c` is padding **[D]**; the 16-bit split (low = plain refs, high = collection count) comes from `taggedRelease`/`getRetainCount` in `OSObject.cpp` **[D]**.

---

### Mechanism

The read at `vptr + 0x558` is out of range for `IOService`, whose table has 169 slots:

```
__ZTV9IOService              = 0xfffffff0071b9a30
__ZTVN9IOService9MetaClassE  = 0xfffffff0071b9f88     (delta 0x558)
vptr = __ZTV9IOService + 16  = 0xfffffff0071b9a40
vptr + 1368                  = 0xfffffff0071b9f98
                             = __ZTVN9IOService9MetaClassE + 16     (exact)
```

Layout: `[16B Itanium header] + [169 slots × 8B = 0x548B] = 0x558B`. So `vptr + 0x558` lands at `+0x10` of the next symbol — the MetaClass vtable's slot 0.

This is the one place worth being precise about three separate objects, because they sit at three different addresses and only the last is an instruction:

| layer | kind | `IOService` value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vtable entry | 8-byte **function pointer** stored in the table | `0xfffffff00bee0c38` |
| function body | **instructions** at that pointer — here one 4-byte `b` | `b 0xfffffff00be69368` |
| branch target | the address the branch reaches | `0xfffffff00be69368` = `~OSMetaClass` |

```
0xfffffff00bee0c38: 0x17fe21cc    b 0xfffffff00be69368     ; __ZN9IOService9MetaClassD1Ev
0xfffffff00bee0c3c: 0x17fe21cb    b 0xfffffff00be69368     ; __ZN9IOService9MetaClassD0Ev
```

The vtable entry holds an address, never an instruction. Everywhere else in this report, "slot 171 points to a wrapper that branches to `~OSMetaClass`" refers to this chain.

Boundary check (`vptr = 0xfffffff0071b9a40`, `__ZTVN9IOService9MetaClassE = 0xfffffff0071b9f88`):

| read | address | relative to `__ZTV::MetaClass` | word there |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| slot 168 (last valid) | `0x71b9f80` | `-0x8` (still `IOService`'s) | `0x0` |
| slot 169 | `0x71b9f88` | `+0x0` — header word 0 (`offset_to_top`) | `0x0` |
| slot 170 | `0x71b9f90` | `+0x8` — header word 1 (`typeinfo`) | `0x0` |
| slot 171 | `0x71b9f98` | `+0x10` — MetaClass slot 0 | `0xfffffff00bee0c38` |
| slot 172 | `0x71b9fa0` | `+0x18` — MetaClass slot 1 | `0xfffffff00bee0c3c` |

---

### Where the dispatch comes from

The faulting function is an internal IOStorageFamily virtual — **slot 169 of eight different vtables** in that kext:

| vtable | slots | slot 169 | slot 171 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0xfffffff005cb3e30` | 188 | `0x497da34` | `0x497c828` |
| `0xfffffff005cb4b60` | 212 | `0x497da34` | `0x496fab4` |
| `0xfffffff005cb56f8` | 190 | `0x497da34` | `0x497c828` |
| `0xfffffff005cb5d98` | 180 | `0x497da34` | `0x4974a6c` |
| `0xfffffff005cb63e8` | 189 | `0x497da34` | `0x497c828` |
| `0xfffffff005cb6a80` | 191 | `0x497da34` | `0x4976c48` |
| `0xfffffff005cb7748` | 183 | `0x497da34` | `0x497c828` |
| `0xfffffff005cb7db0` | 180 | `0x497da34` | `0xbfcce7c` |

All eight have ≥180 slots, so `#0x558` is a **legal** offset for the kext's own classes — slot 171 is a real, distinct function pointer in each. The kext is not out of bounds with respect to its own hierarchy; it only is if the object handed in has fewer than 172 slots.

The expected receiver therefore has ≥172 virtual slots; the actual object has 169. That is the mismatch, and `IOService` fits it exactly.

Three supporting facts, and their limits:

- **No direct entry.** Scanning `__TEXT_EXEC`, `__PLK_TEXT_EXEC`, `__PRELINK_TEXT` and `__KLD` for `bl`/`b` with an immediate targeting `0x497da34` gives zero hits; a scan for `adrp`/`add` pairs materialising that address also gives zero. This rules out a direct branch and a statically materialised address, not every indirect path.
- **`x24` is not reloaded.** Only two instructions touch it: `stp x24, x23, [sp, #64]` (spill) and `mov x24, x0`. So the object whose vptr is loaded is the incoming `x0`, and `mov x0, x24` passes that same object as `this`.
- **The function's intent.** Its only `adrp`/`add` resolves to `0xfffffff00497daec`, a code address (a callback), not a string. It builds a small stack structure (`stp xzr,xzr,[sp]`, `str xzr,[sp,#16]`, `strb wzr,[sp,#4]`, `stp x26,x8,[sp,#24]`, `str x19,[sp,#40]`) and passes `sp+24` as `x5`. So a callback/context struct is passed alongside the receiver. The Apple-side method name is unidentified: `LC_SYMTAB` is `(0,0,0,0)` and `__cstring` holds only log format strings.

**Root cause (static, confirmed):** the tree's link layout places `<Class>::MetaClass` vtable immediately after the class vtable, so an out-of-range slot read on a 169-slot class lands on a virtual destructor instead of on inert data.

**Unconfirmed:** the dynamic type of `x24`. If the receiver really were one of the eight kext classes, `#0x558` would resolve inside its own 180–212-slot table and nothing would fault. The crash requires a receiver with <172 slots; `IOService` fits, but a fit is not proof. The panic record has no dereferenceable `x24`, the kext's `LC_SYMTAB` is empty, and the eight vtables' metaclass pointers live in `__DATA.__common`/`__bss` and read `0x0` on disk, so their owning classes cannot be named either.

Candidate explanations, none excluded:

1. the receiver really is an `IOService`-family object (type confusion, or a legitimate-but-wrong object passed down);
2. `vptr` was overwritten before the call (use-after-free / stale object), so `[x24]` yields a foreign table;
3. `x24` is right but the vptr was retargeted during a pending destruction;
4. an unrelated upstream defect fires first, and the layout only decides where it lands.

`far = 0x3000c` is *consistent with* an ordinary `OSObject`-layout instance (`+8` holding a plausible `retainCount`), which mildly favours (1); it does not identify the vptr.

**Decisive follow-up:** at fault time dump `x24`, `[x24]`, and the first 16 bytes at `[x24]`; compare `[x24]` against `0xfffffff0071b9a40` (`__ZTV9IOService + 16`) and against the eight IOStorageFamily vptr values (`vtable + 16`, list above). That single dump separates (1) from (2)/(3).

---

### Comparison with the stock kernelcache

Against the stock kernelcache pinned by the same OS profile, `f18b4df865405f2a287b84977d7aca745e056d656d9fc9df1662970ce2969de7`.

For the `vptr+1368` read, three things are distinct: **(A)** the address read, **(B)** the 8-byte value stored there — what `blr` jumps to, **(C)** what is at the address in (B), and whether it is executable.

| | Apple stock 21H461 | this build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__ZTV9IOService` | `0xfffffff0071a1bf0` | `0xfffffff0071b9a30` |
| `vptr` (`__ZTV + 16`) | `0xfffffff0071a1c00` | `0xfffffff0071b9a40` |
| `__ZTVN9IOService9MetaClassE` | `0xfffffff007161d88` | `0xfffffff0071b9f88` |
| distance `__ZTV` → its MetaClass vtable | `-0x3fe68` (well before) | `+0x558` (immediately after) |
| vtable span / function slots | `0x558` / **169** (0..168) | `0x558` / **169** (0..168) |
| slot 168 | `0x0` | `0x0` |
| address point + 16-byte header (`offset_to_top`, `typeinfo`, both `0`) | same | same |
| **(A)** address read | `0xfffffff0071a2158` (`__DATA_CONST`) | `0xfffffff0071b9f98` (`__ZTV::MetaClass + 16`) |
| **(B)** 8-byte value stored | `0xfffffff0079401f8` | `0xfffffff00bee0c38` |
| **(B′)** symbol at that value | `__ZN9OSBoolean10gMetaClassE` — a *data* object | `__ZN9IOService9MetaClassD1Ev` — a *function* |
| **(C)** where `blr` lands | `__DATA` + `0x781f8`, past that segment's `filesize` of `0x24000` → **BSS, non-executable** | `__TEXT_EXEC`, executable, first instruction `b 0xfffffff00be69368` |

Both builds read at the same relative offset (`+0x568` from `__ZTV`, past a `0x558`-byte table); only the contents differ. Stock's stored value is a normal VA, not a fixup-encoded pointer — that kernelcache has neither `LC_DYLD_CHAINED_FIXUPS` nor `LC_DYLD_INFO` (checked by enumerating its load commands).

Stock is not immunized by this — it is the same out-of-range read, landing on `__DATA` instead of another vtable. The value is **not** zero, and a `blr` to that non-executable address would still be an invalid target; there is no boot log showing whether it ever happens, so its actual behaviour is unknown. What differs is only the landing zone.

So the count/length claim is bounded:

> The `IOService` vtable has the same slot count and terminator position as Apple's stock kernelcache. The observed failure is not explained by missing `IOService` virtual slots or a difference in its vtable length.

We do **not** claim full ABI equivalence. The 169 function pointers were not compared element-by-element, so only count, terminator position and address point are shown to agree. Two differences are already visible (distance to the MetaClass vtable; the nature of what sits at `vptr+0x558`).

Adding `OSMetaClassDeclareReserved*` to `IOService` was considered and rejected: on iOS targets `APPLE_KEXT_VTABLE_PADDING == 0` (`OSMetaClass.h:165-166`), so those macros expand to nothing and occupy zero slots — the symbol table contains no `_RESERVED` symbols.

**Three stock classes share the same `0x558` adjacency:**

| class | stock `__ZTV` | stock `::MetaClass` | delta | **(B)** value at slot 171 | **(C)** where it points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `IOResources` | `0x7162440` | `0x7162998` | `0x558` | `0x77c5260` | inside `IOResources::getWorkLoop` (`+0x7c4`) |
| `IOPowerConnection` | `0x719ea08` | `0x719ef60` | `0x558` | `0x785451c` | inside `IOPowerConnection::getMetaClass` (`+0xc`) |
| `IORootParent` | `0x71a27e0` | `0x71a2d38` | `0x558` | `0x7872460` | inside `IOPMrootDomain::removePublishedFeature` (`+0x9d0`) |

Verified for `IOResources`: `0x7162450 + 171*8 == 0x7162998 + 16`, i.e. stock's slot 171 also reads its own MetaClass vtable's slot 0; the same arithmetic holds for the other two. All three targets are interior addresses of real functions, not entry points, so a `blr` there would be execution from an interior address — an invalid control-flow target rather than a resolvable call. All three happen to start with an instruction sequence resembling a prologue (`stp x22,x21,[sp,#-48]!`), which does not make them entry points. This is static and structural: there is no runtime evidence that any of the three ever fired.

---

### Observed trigger sequence

The sequence under which the crash was seen — not a minimal reproduction, and not a claim that an arbitrary `IOService` subclass reproduces it:

1. a class deriving from `IOService` creates an `IOMedia` in `start()` and calls `registerService()`;
2. that triggers `IOMediaBSDClient::start()` → `createNodes()`;
3. the class's `__ZTV<Class>` and `__ZTVN<Class>9MetaClassE` sit exactly `0x558` apart, so slot 171 points to a wrapper that branches to `~OSMetaClass`;
4. data abort at `~OSMetaClass + 0x24` with a reproducible `far`.

Step 3 is a layout property of this build, not a consequence of step 1. The class that owns the storage publication path here, `NativeUfsBlock` (`__ZTV = 0xfffffff007204098`, `__ZTVN14NativeUfsBlock9MetaClassE = 0xfffffff0072045f0`, gap `0x558`), is one of the 19, so the precondition holds for it. Whether a newly written `IOService` subclass acquires the same adjacency depends on where the linker places the two tables.

---

### Suggested direction (open for discussion — not a validated fix)

**1.** Separate the two tables so an out-of-range read leaves the vtable area. Stock does this for `IOService` by putting the MetaClass vtable `-0x3fe68` away, so `vptr+1368` lands on `__ZN9OSBoolean10gMetaClassE`. That is not by itself safe — the address is still non-executable — but it does not reach a destructor.

**2. Guarded poison tail (alternative, unvalidated).** Append slots pointing at a `brk` trap after the last real virtual.

- A single slot is insufficient: the reproduced dispatch uses index **171** on a 169-slot class, so at least slots **169, 170, 171** must be covered.
- Coverage is not universal — a caller compiled against a 212-slot class uses slot 212 (`+0x6a0`), which a 3-slot tail misses.
- ABI impact unverified: appending at the tail should leave the address point (`+0x10`) and RTTI alone, but it moves every following symbol and needs re-validation of derived-class slot offsets.
- Whether the current linker/layout stage can express this is unknown to us.

**Where the layout is decided.** Not `emit_prelink.py`: it copies `__DATA_CONST` byte-for-byte at the original offsets and preserves `va == original + slide` (`:183-204`), with no symbol ordering or per-symbol padding, and never touches `__ZTV`. `__ZTV<Class>` and `__ZTVN<Class>9MetaClassE` are both emitted by `OSDefineMetaClassWithInit` (`OSMetaClass.h:2021-2034`) into `(__DATA_CONST,__const)`; both stock and this build use that section and differ only in ordering within it. Which mechanism produces that ordering is not established.

---

### Environment

- XNU `xnu-10063.141.1` (`feeds.toml`)
- OS profile `ipados-17.7.11-21H461`; stock kernelcache sha256 `f18b4df8…`
- Device: Xiaomi Pad 5 Pro Wi-Fi (`elish`, SM8250-AC), `cpus=1`
- Build artifact: `kernel.macho` sha256 `48814ac0c81f8b40a079de8fd614a6e0e61e0fd8fb0d5a009c9220020b9e3848`

We already worked around it on the device side (the driver registers `bdevsw` itself and bypasses `IOMedia`/`IOMediaBSDClient`), so this is not blocking us.

---

### Open questions

**Blocking**

1. **Dynamic type of `x24`** — decides whether the receiver is an `IOService`-family object or something else. *Collect:* at fault time, `x24`, `[x24]`, 16 bytes at `[x24]`; compare against `0xfffffff0071b9a40` and the eight kext vptr values.
2. **Was `[x24]` overwritten before the call?** — stale/overwritten vptr vs wrong-object pass. *Collect:* same dump; a vptr matching no known `__ZTV+16` indicates corruption.
3. **Is there an upstream trigger independent of layout?** — the landing zone is explained, the out-of-range *dispatch* is not. *Collect:* the caller chain reaching slot 169 — construction site and the code handing the object to the kext.

**Non-blocking**

4. Name of the function at `0xfffffff00497da34` — `LC_SYMTAB` is `(0,0,0,0)`, `__cstring` holds only log format strings.
5. Which classes own the eight IOStorageFamily vtables — metaclass pointers are in `__DATA.__common`/`__bss` and read `0x0` on disk. Knowing this would show whether an `IOService`-family receiver was ever legal for that call.
6. Is slot 171 ever dispatched on the other 18 classes? *Collect:* `brk` instrumentation or a breakpoint on the eight kext slot-169 functions, logging `[x24]` across several boots.
7. Do the 169 `IOService` pointers match stock slot-for-slot? Not compared; mechanically possible since that kernelcache has no chained fixups.
8. What would stock actually do at slot 171? No boot log either way.
9. Does a poison tail affect RTTI or derived-class layouts? Untested.
10. What produces the ordering difference at link time? Unverified; we only establish `emit_prelink.py` is not the cause.
11. Why is stock's MetaClass slot 0 a complete function body while ours is a 4-byte branch? Possibly `-Os`/ICF; unverified.

### 中文摘要

本树产出的内核里，**176 个类中有 170 个**把 `__ZTV<Class>` 与自己的 `__ZTV<Class>::MetaClass` 紧邻放在 `(__DATA_CONST,__const)`（Apple 原厂为 75/135）。

其中 **19 个类**两张表的间距恰为 `0x558`，这正好是类 vtable 自身的总跨度。因此在任一这些类上按第 171 号槽读取，落点就是 **MetaClass vtable 的第一项** —— `<Class>::MetaClassD1Ev`（MetaClass 完整对象析构入口）。19 个类逐一核对，**19/19 均跳转到 `~OSMetaClass`（`0xfffffff00be69368`）**。

19 个类中只有 `IOService` 连接到了真机观测到的崩溃；其余 18 个表结构与崩溃路径同样已验证，但没有运行时证据表明分派真的到达过它们。

**根因（静态已确证）**：本树的链接布局把 `<Class>::MetaClass` vtable 紧贴在类 vtable 之后，于是对 169 槽的类做越界槽读取时，落点是一个虚析构，而不是无害数据。

**尚未确证**：`x24` 的动态类型。若 receiver 真是那 8 个 kext 类之一，`#0x558` 会落在其自身 180–212 槽表内，不会崩。崩溃要求 receiver 少于 172 槽；`IOService` 正好吻合，但吻合不等于证明。panic 记录无可解引用的 `x24`，kext 符号已剥离，8 个 vtable 的 metaclass 指针在 `.bss` 运行时才填充，故连它们属于哪个类都无法命名。

**与原厂对照**：两边都是 169 槽、槽 168 都空终止、address point 一致，故「本故障不由 `IOService` 虚函数槽缺失或 vtable 长度差异解释」。但**不**声称已排除全部 ABI 差异——169 个函数指针未逐项比对。

原厂并非免疫：它做的是**同样的越界读**，只是落在 `__DATA`（`OSBoolean::gMetaClass` 数据地址）。该值**不是 0**，且 `blr` 到不可执行地址仍属非法目标；无启动日志说明是否实际发生，故其真实行为未知。差别只在落点。

另需说明：`emit_prelink.py` **不是**布局成因——它按原偏移逐字节拷贝 `__DATA_CONST` 并保持 `va == original + slide`，不做符号排序；顺序在上游链接阶段就已确定。

修复方向给出两条，均未验证：(1) 把两张表分开，使越界读离开 vtable 区域；(2) 尾部 poison 区——**至少需 3 槽**（覆盖 169/170/171），且覆盖不普遍（212 槽的调用方会用到 `+0x6a0`），ABI 影响与当前链接层能否实现**均未验证**，仅作待讨论备选。

我们已在设备侧用自注册 `bdevsw` 绕开，**当前不构成阻塞**。

issues.title: chat: closed side panel slides out and back on its own on desktop (trackpad-swipe drag, v0.12.0+)
issues.body:
### Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already reported.

### KiroCrew version

0.12.1 (packaged build). First seen on 0.12.0.

### Release channel

Stable

### How is it installed?

Not sure

### Platform

Linux — AL2023 (gateway). The dashboard runs in Chrome 157.0.8103.39 (64-bit) on Windows 11, on a separate machine, over a remote tunnel. It is a plain browser tab, not the desktop app, so no finger-down or lift-off phases are reported.

### What happened

On the chat page, with the right side panel closed, the panel slides out about 20 to 50 px and slides back a moment later. It happens several times an hour with no deliberate input: no hover near the panel, no click on the toggle, no swipe. The machine has no touchscreen, and a deliberate sideways tilt of the mouse wheel does not reproduce it. It started after the update to 0.12.0, the first release that contains the desktop trackpad drag from #25755.

Two console captures show two separate triggers:

| Trigger | What precedes the slide | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Sideways wheel stream | A run of `wheel` events with positive `deltaX` that decays smoothly (72.5, 31.7, 3.3, 2.5, 1.7, 0.8 ...), with no deliberate scroll by the reporter | 10:48:39 |
| Window regains focus | A `focus` event on the window, then the panel is mounted, restyled for about 0.5 s, and removed. No sideways wheel event in the window | 10:56:29, 10:56:53 |

Mechanism for the first trigger, at v0.12.1:

- `website/src/hooks/useTrackpadSwipe.ts:259-271`: the first event of a run starts a drag whenever `|dx| > |dy|` and `wants(dir)` agrees. There is no minimum size and no check that the stream comes from a trackpad.
- `website/src/pages/chat/page/chatTrackpadSwipe.ts:154`: `wants('left')` is true whenever the panel is closed, so any positive `deltaX` run starts an open drag. It falls back below the 20% commit line, which is the "pop and return" the reporter sees.

Mechanism for the second trigger: unknown. No cited source path is established. The capture shows the panel column added and removed with no wheel input after a window focus event.

Expected: a closed side panel stays closed unless the person opens it, by the toggle, the shortcut, or a deliberate swipe.

Actual: it slides partly out and back after small or stray sideways wheel input, and after the window regains focus.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a chat on desktop with the side panel docked right and closed.
2. Keep the page in a browser where the OS or input driver sends smooth sideways `wheel` momentum (here, the source could not be pinned down while the reporter's hands were off the mouse).
3. Wait, or switch to another window and back.
4. Watch the right edge: the panel slides out a few dozen px and returns.

Frequency: several times an hour across 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10. Captured: one clear event of the first trigger, two of the second.

### Relevant log output

Console capture around the first trigger. A capture-phase `wheel` listener logged each non-zero `deltaX`, and a `MutationObserver` logged changes to the `side-panel-*` elements. Timestamps are local.

```shell
10:48:39.361  sideways scroll 72.5
10:48:39.579  [panel-watch] (side panel change)
10:48:39.579  [panel-watch] (side panel change)
10:48:39.582  [panel-watch] (side panel change)
10:48:39.608  sideways scroll 31.666669845581055
10:48:39.613  [panel-watch] (side panel change)
10:48:39.631  sideways scroll 3.3333334922790527
10:48:39.670  sideways scroll 2.5
10:48:39.689  sideways scroll 2.5
10:48:39.720  sideways scroll 1.6666667461395264
10:48:39.749  sideways scroll 0.8333333730697632
10:48:39.774  sideways scroll 0.8333333730697632
10:48:39.888  sideways scroll 0.8333333730697632
10:48:39.908  sideways scroll 1.6666667461395264
10:48:40.055  sideways scroll 0.8333333730697632
10:48:40.391  sideways scroll 0.8333333730697632
10:48:40.704  [panel-watch] (last side panel change of the run)
```

Second trigger. The window logger and the panel observer ran in the same page, and no `wheel` event with `deltaX` was logged in this window:

```shell
15:56:29.743  {what: 'window focus'}
15:56:30.320  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:30.581  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:30.808  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:30.935  {what: 'panel removed', detail: 'side-panel-column'}
15:56:53.623  {what: 'window focus'}
15:56:56.654  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:56.953  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:57.192  {what: 'panel style'}
15:56:57.364  {what: 'panel removed', detail: 'side-panel-column'}
```

The second block's clock is UTC; the first block's is local (UTC-5).

### Anything else

- Regression window: first seen after updating to 0.12.0 on 2026-11-06. The reporter never saw it on earlier releases. Still present on 0.12.1. No commit after v0.12.1 touches `chatTrackpadSwipe.ts` or `useTrackpadSwipe.ts`.
- Source of the sideways wheel stream: a third capture recorded it in detail. Every event is `isTrusted: true`, `deltaMode` 0, `deltaY` 0, no Shift held, and the pointer had not moved for 5 to 10 seconds before it. So the input comes from the OS or the input device, not from a page script, and arrives while the person is not touching the mouse. The mouse is a Logitech MX Master 3S, which has a horizontal thumb wheel; a single 100 px step and a smoothed burst summing to about 90 px both fit that wheel, but the device was not isolated as the source. That capture did not record panel changes, so it does not show whether those runs moved the panel.

```shell
11:23:32.960  wheel dx=54.17 dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5098

11:23:33.043  wheel dx=2.5   dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5182

11:23:33.076  wheel dx=1.67  dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5215

11:23:33.126  wheel dx=0.83  dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5264
11:23:33.144  wheel dx=0.83  dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5282

11:23:33.193  wheel dx=0.83  dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5331
11:23:33.260  wheel dx=0.83  dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=message-bubble msSinceMouseMove=5398
13:25:46.466  wheel dx=100   dy=0 mode=0 trusted=true shift=false over=input-wrapper  msSinceMouseMove=10357 msSinceKey=9354
```
- Workaround: docking the side panel at the bottom turns the drag off (`enabled` requires `sidePanelDock === 'right'`). This does not address the focus trigger.
- Suggested fix: add a setting to turn the desktop trackpad drag off on the chat page, and require a minimum distance (for example the existing 80 px `SWIPE_THRESHOLD_PX`) before a closed panel starts to follow, so stray momentum cannot move it. Alternative: start a drag only once the desktop app's finger-down phase has been heard, and keep the current behavior in a plain browser behind the setting.
- Focus trigger: separately, a window `focus` should not mount and animate a closed panel.
- Not a duplicate: #25755 added the behavior; #27419 is a similar stray-swipe fix for the Bots tabs on the Mates page; #30618 covers touch phones, not desktop. Other searches with no relevant hits: "side panel opens itself", "activity panel flicker", "side panel flash focus", "horizontal scroll opens side panel".
