issues.title: [Bug]: owed-restart obligation can never clear when one gateway PID is recorded both mapped and stopped_unmapped
issues.body:
## Bug Description

After an update that ended with a fleet restart, every CLI invocation keeps printing:

```
⚠ A previous `hermes update` pulled new code but did not restart running gateways.
  Gateways may still be serving pre-update modules (mixed sys.modules).
  Run `hermes update` or `hermes gateway restart`.
```

The warning is wrong: the gateway was restarted and its runtime status reports
`code_sha = <checkout HEAD>`, `code_version = 0.22.5`. It cannot be cleared by restarting, because the
host obligation (`~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/host-update-restart-<install>.json`) records the
same gateway PID twice — once mapped, once as an unmapped stop — and
`_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` can never satisfy both entries.

Recorded inventory (verbatim, from the record this host kept armed after a successful restart):

```json
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": "default", "pid": 912, "supervisor": "launchd",
 "code_sha": "4d04303818b61bf3aa09278af48356315515965b", "code_version": "0.22.4",
 "restart_via": "launchd", "detail": {}}
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": null, "pid": 912, "stopped_unmapped": true}
{"kind": "gateway", "profile": "default", "pid": 8555, "supervisor": "launchd",
 "code_sha": "bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e", "code_version": "0.22.5",
 "restart_via": "launchd", "detail": {}}
```

Same PID (912) appears as an identified gateway and as `stopped_unmapped`. The record also carries a
`restarted` stamp for the expected SHA, which the readers do not consult.

## Steps to Reproduce

Deterministic, without needing a real update — the obligation is public API
(`hermes_cli/update_host_obligation.write_host_obligation`):

1. Have one launchd-supervised gateway, live, on the checkout HEAD (`hermes gateway status` → current).
2. Arm the obligation with an inventory that names that live gateway once mapped and once as
   `{"kind": "gateway", "profile": null, "pid": <same pid>, "stopped_unmapped": true}`
   (this is the shape `_record_owed_gateway_inventory` produces when the unmapped sweep stops a PID
   that the update plan already knew as a mapped profile gateway).
3. `hermes gateway restart -y` — the gateway comes back on HEAD, `gateway_state.json` shows the
   correct `code_sha`.
4. Every `hermes --version` / `hermes gateway status` / `hermes auth list` still prints the ⚠ block.
5. `_fleet_restart_obligation_armed()` stays `True` and `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` stays `False`
   forever. Only `clear_host_obligation()` silences it.

Note: run the probe with `hermes-agent/venv/bin/python`. The launcher interpreter
(`~/.hermes/tools/python-<ver>/python3`, no `ruamel.yaml`) and `/usr/bin/python3` (too old) hit the
`try/except` in `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` and return an *empty* fleet, which looks like a
second, unrelated failure while debugging.

## Expected Behavior

After the fleet is proven current on the pulled SHA, the obligation discharges and the warning stops —
even when the inventory contains an `stopped_unmapped` row for a PID that no longer exists (and even
more so when that PID is the same one an identified row already covers).

## Actual Behavior

The warning is permanent. The mapped entry is covered by the live gateway; the unmapped entry has no
identity to match, and the rule below refuses to let a live gateway be its successor because the
mapped entry already explains it — `covered - owed` is empty, so the function returns `False` on every
check:

`hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:430` (v0.22.5)

```python
if owed and _UNMAPPED_GATEWAY in owed and not (_fleet_covered_gateways(
        [row for row in fleet if not row_is_external(row)]) or set()) - owed:
    # An unmapped stopped gateway has no identity to match, so only a local gateway that no
    # mapped owed one explains can be its successor; another checkout's gateway never is.
    return False
```

## Affected Component

- Other: update / fleet-restart bookkeeping (CLI startup warning)

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 26A434), launchd-supervised gateway
- Hermes: v0.22.5, commit `bf0203a794a07aac3ff764972ab9087baa4e4f4e`, install method git
- Python: 3.14.9 (launcher) / 3.11.16 (`hermes-agent/venv`) — reproduces with the venv interpreter
- Single profile (`default`), one gateway, no serve/dashboard runtimes

## Root Cause Analysis

1. `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet_verify.py:132 _record_owed_gateway_inventory()` builds the owed set as
   *mapped gateways from the update plan* + *one `stopped_unmapped` row per PID from
   `restart.stopped_unmapped_pids`*. There is no de-duplication: when the unmapped sweep in
   `update_cmd_fleet.py` stops a PID that the plan already knew as a mapped profile gateway (the
   `profile_processes` / `unrestartable_pids` path), the same physical process is owed twice.
2. `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:303 _marker_owed_gateways()` turns the mapped row into
   `("gateway", "default")` and the `stopped_unmapped` row into `_UNMAPPED_GATEWAY`.
3. `_marker_only_restart_obsolete()` (`hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py:354`) requires every owed
   identity to be covered by the live fleet, and additionally (line 430) requires that the live
   gateway covering the unmapped obligation is *not* one a mapped owed entry already explains. With a
   single gateway both conditions can never hold at once → fail-closed deadlock. The `restarted`
   stamp written by a successful restart is never read by this path.

## Proposed Fix

Either (or both) of these, both local to the bookkeeping:

1. **De-duplicate at write time** (`_record_owed_gateway_inventory`, `update_cmd_fleet_verify.py:132`):
   drop a `stopped_unmapped` row whose PID already appears in the mapped rows — the process is
   already named, so a second obligation adds nothing:

   ```python
   mapped_pids = {row["pid"] for row in rows if row.get("profile")}
   rows = [row for row in rows if row.get("profile") or row.get("pid") not in mapped_pids]
   ```

2. **Or discharge at read time** (`_marker_only_restart_obsolete`, `update_cmd_fleet.py:430`): treat a
   live gateway at HEAD as the successor of an unmapped row when the unmapped PID is one an owed
   mapped row already names (same PID), instead of requiring an unrelated local gateway.

The first is the cleaner fix: an unmapped row only carries information for a process nothing else
named.

## Workaround

Clear the record once its debt is provably paid — `expected_sha` equals checkout HEAD and every live
runtime is `current` on that SHA — via `hermes_cli.update_host_obligation.clear_host_obligation()`.
Back up the JSON first. A daily watchdog script that applies exactly that check and otherwise leaves
the obligation alone keeps the warning from accumulating.

issues.title: sessions_read 签发侧未接（锁没有锁眼）+ narrowed_principal fail-open + 桥侧方案
issues.body:
## 背景

外部贡献者（未具名）翻源码后发现：`Principal.sessions_read` 的**读侧**执行已落地，但**签发侧还没接**，
并顺手发现一处 **fail-open**。我逐条核实，四条全部成立（另补一条 Rust 侧遗漏）。

他们的原话：**「这枚锁现在还没有锁眼」**——准确。

## 一、四条核实结果（全部实测/读码确认）

| # | 说法 | 核实 | 证据 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 读侧执行已落地（0.9.18） | ✅ **成立** | `mdcos.py:4655-4658`（`_sr = getattr(getattr(self, "principal", None), "sessions_read", None)`），且有守卫 `test_issue712_session_window_attribution` 的 **E1–E4**（含 `sessions_read=["*"]` 全读不收窄） |
| **2** | 签发侧没接 | ✅ **成立** | `tokens.issue()` 参数：`role, actor, clearance, tenant, ttl, label, issued_by, parent, delegable, layers_allow, ops_allow, path, _authorized_by, _allow_bootstrap`——**无 `sessions_read`**；`tokens.derive()` 参数：`parent_token, role, actor, ttl, label, path, clearance, layers_allow, ops_allow`——**同样没有** |
| **3** | `narrowed_principal` fail-open | ✅ **成立** | 见 §二 |
| **4** | （我补的）Rust 侧未实现 | ⚠️ **成立** | `grep sessions_read rust/` → **0 命中**，与 Python 侧不一致 |

## 二、#3 的定性：不是「忘传一个参数」

`tokens.py` 的 `narrowed_principal`（约 836 行起）构造 `Principal` 时：

```python
q = Principal(
    tenant=p.tenant, actor=p.actor, session=p.session, harness=p.harness,
    unit=u, role=u,
    clearance=_clamp_level(spec["clearance_cap"], p.clearance),
    can_write=bool(spec["can_write"]) and bool(p.can_write),
    can_admin=False,
    layers_allow=_narrow(spec["layers_allow"], p.layers_allow),   # ← 收窄了
    ops_allow=_narrow(spec["ops_allow"], p.ops_allow),            # ← 收窄了
    token_id=p.token_id, parent=p.parent, expires_at=p.expires_at,
    auth_mode=p.auth_mode,
    theory_ok=p.theory_ok, theory_version=p.theory_version)      # ← 漏了 sessions_read
```

`Principal.sessions_read` 缺省是 `None`（＝不限制）⇒ **带读面限制的 owner 走 `as_unit` 请求级收窄后，
读面静默变宽**，与「收窄只能变小」的设计初衷直接冲突。

**但根因不是"忘了传一个参数"**，而是：

> **`narrowed_principal` 的收窄语义只覆盖了两个字段，`sessions_read` 是第三个收窄维度，
> 加字段时没有同步收窄面。**

⇒ 所以修复时**应同时审计**：还有哪些**收窄型**字段（而不是"所有字段"）没被 `narrowed_principal` 收窄。
现存的收窄型面：`clearance` / `can_write` / `can_admin` / `layers_allow` / `ops_allow` / **`sessions_read`（缺）**。

## 三、桥侧方案（对外部提问的回答：`session→token` 映射 vs 请求级带会话身份）

**结论：请求级带会话身份，但必须挂在 `sessions_read` 之下。**

### 3.1 为什么不做 `session→token` 映射

需求场景是「**全家几条 AI 共用一个 profile**，不想为分房各起一套库」——
这正是 `as_unit` 的设计动机（`mcp_server.call_tool` 的 `as_unit` 参数，注释写着「**单进程多身份**」）。

⇒ `session→token` 映射要为每条 AI 签发一枚令牌 ⇒ 一个 profile 变 N 套凭据，反而更重。

### 3.2 但 `as_session` 与 `as_unit` 有**本质差异**（这是关键）

`narrowed_principal` 的 docstring 原文：

> 「因为收窄是**单调的**，调用方伪造 `as_unit` 的最坏结果等于不传（owner 全权），
> **不可能提权** —— 这是本机制不需要对 `as_unit` 额外鉴权的根据。」

⇒ **`as_unit` 免鉴权，是因为它是收窄**（换单元只能变小）。

⇒ **而裸的 `as_session` 不是收窄**：换 session 是**平权**（A 条 AI 换成 B 条，权限一样）⇒ **伪造就能读别人的**。

⇒ **所以裸 `as_session` 会开一个比 #3 更大的 fail-open。**

### 3.3 正解

```
token 签发：  sessions_read = ["sessA", "sessB"]      ← 锁眼
请求时：      as_session = "sessA"
                ↓
              必须在 sessions_read 内，否则 TokenError（fail-closed）
                ↓
              「从允许集合里选一个」= 仍是收窄 ⇒ 安全性仍来自单调性
```

⇒ 效果：**一个 profile、一枚令牌**；**每条 AI 只读自己的**；**伪造最坏 = 选错一个（仍在授权范围内）**。

## 四、工作项（按依赖顺序）

| # | 事项 | 依赖 | 规模 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | `tokens.issue()` / `tokens.derive()` 加 `sessions_read`；`derive` 按**交集收窄**（复用 `_narrow`）；落盘 `rec` 存该字段 | — | 小（外部贡献者已有约 60 行草稿） |
| **B** | CLI 加 `--sessions-read` | A | 小 |
| **C** | 修 `narrowed_principal` 的 fail-open（`sessions_read=_narrow(p.sessions_read, ...)` 或直接传导） | A | 极小 |
| **D** | **审计 `narrowed_principal` 的全部收窄型字段**（防同类漏项） | C | 小 |
| **E** | **`as_session` 请求级入口** + 「必须在 `sessions_read` 内」校验 | A | 中 |
| **F** | Rust 侧同步（`grep sessions_read rust/` = 0） | A–E | 待评估 |

⚠️ **C 和 E 不可只做一半**：只做 C（修 fail-open）而不做 E，用户仍然"读各归各"用不上；
只做 E 而不做 C，`as_unit` 仍会把读面放大。

## 五、可测断言（建议）

| # | 断言 | 怎么让它红 |
|---|---|---|
| **T1** | `issue(sessions_read=["s1"])` 后落盘 rec 含该字段 | 不传则不落盘 ⇒ 读 rec 断言 |
| **T2** | `derive(parent_token, sessions_read=["s2"])` 得**交集**（空集 ⇒ 报错，不得变成"不限制"） | 传入**超集**，断言结果 ≤ 父 |
| **T3** | `narrowed_principal(p_with_sessions_read, unit)` 结果**保留** `sessions_read` 且不宽于 p | 删掉传导 ⇒ 结果 None ⇒ 红 |
| **T4** | `as_session="s_not_in_read"` ⇒ **报错**，不得静默退回不限制 | 传未授权 session |
| **T5** | `sessions_read=["*"]` 时 `as_session` 任意值可通过（全读语义） | — |
| **T6** | `sessions_read=None`（旧行为）时 `as_session` 不传也能正常读（向后兼容） | — |

## 六、诚实边界

1. **我未验证外部贡献者那 60 行草稿**（尚未提交）；`derive` 用交集收窄与 N123 过期夹紧同构，**方向我认为对**，但需看代码；
2. **Rust 侧是否应同步未定**——需先确认 Rust 是否参与读路径鉴权；
3. **不解决「同一个 session 内多条 AI 互相读」**——本 issue 只做 session 粒度；
4. **`as_session` 的鉴权模型只在 `sessions_read` 内成立**，若将来 `sessions_read` 支持通配/正则，需重新论证单调性。

issues.title: `UniXNU-sheng` cannot build on a clean checkout: `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json` is required but no repository ships it
issues.body:
`./unixnu build kernel -D ../UniXNU-sheng` stops at archive-10 on a clean checkout because
`scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` requires `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json`, which is
produced only by `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` — and that script needs staged qualification
evidence (a specific prelinked candidate, two live `gdb-stop.json` snapshots and a KDK reference)
that cannot be produced from a clean tree, and is not in any repository.
`build-software-aes-bindings.py` already falls back to a recorded result for exactly this situation
(`scripts/data/native-aes-original-bindings.S`). Could the storage audit get the same treatment, or
could the audit record itself be published?
## Environment
| | |
| --- | --- |
| UniXNU | `ae687009348296e97e49ce6e925795044f363ce6` |
| UniXNU-sheng | `08cde20edc32` |
| OS profile | `ipados-17.7.11-21H461` (`[kernel.prelink] kernelcache_sha256 = f18b4df865405f2a287b84977d7aca745e056d656d9fc9df1662970ce2969de7`) |
| Host | macOS 26.7.1, Intel i5-9600KF (x86_64, 6 cores), Xcode 26.5, Python 3.15.1 |
| QEMU | `qemu-system-aarch64` (TCG; HVF is Apple-Silicon-only, so TCG is the only option here) |
## Reproduction
```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU
git clone https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng
cd UniXNU
./unixnu defconfig sheng_defconfig -D ../UniXNU-sheng
./unixnu build kernel -D ../UniXNU-sheng
```
## Actual result
`archive-06` (AES) passes with `PASS: native AES bound with the recorded original-kernelcache addresses`.
`archive-10` fails with a raw traceback:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../tree/scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py", line 20, in <module>
    audit = json.loads((ROOT / 'build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json').read_text())
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  '.../tree/build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json'
```
The same failure should occur on `macos-26` in the documented workflow, whose default dispatch is
`UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng` + `sheng_defconfig` + `steps=kernel`:
```sh
gh workflow run macos.yml -f device_repository=UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng -f defconfig=sheng_defconfig -f steps=kernel
```
## Why a clean tree cannot produce it
1. `sheng_defconfig` enables `CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=y` and `CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=y`,
   and `[kernel] archives` places the two `build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` entries after
   `component:VirtioMmioBlock` / `component:RamBlock`. The builder reads the audit unconditionally.
2. The kernel step's `storage-headers` pass only prepares headers:
   `scripts/prepare-storage-headers.py` writes `build/storage-abi/headers.json` with
   `qualification: false`, and its own docstring says the audit "additionally needs the live guest
   metadata snapshot and the original kernel candidate".
3. `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` has no CLI and hardcodes its inputs:
   - `build/xnu-prelink/native-apfs-load-positive.macho` + `.json`
   - `build/darwinboot-storage-native-metadata/gdb-stop.json` (must match `kernel_sha256`, must carry
     `TCR_EL1`/`SCTLR_EL1`/`TTBR0_EL1`/`TTBR1_EL1` and 0x50-byte dumps at both metaclass addresses)
   - `build/image4-ignition/aes-interface-audit.json`
   The candidate is itself the output of a prelink, which runs *after* the archives, so the chain
   cannot bootstrap itself.
4. `/build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:2`), so the artifact exists only in a workspace where the
   qualification was actually performed.
I searched for it rather than assuming: the string `abstract_complete_destructors_trap` (written only
by this audit) appears in the repository only in `scripts/audit-storage-interface.py` and
`scripts/build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py`; it is absent from `UniXNU-sheng`,
`UniXNU-sm8550-common`, `profiles/`, and from every tree fetched by `unixnu fetch`.
`git log -S 'interface-audit.json'` returns only the initial import and one docs commit — no data file
was ever added.
`docs/porting/migration.md` ("sheng build inputs") does list `storage-abi/interface-audit.json` as a
required input, so this looks like an intentional local input — but it is currently a hard blocker
for anyone building `sheng` from source, including CI.
## Precedent for a fix
`scripts/build-software-aes-bindings.py` already does the right thing when the qualification evidence
is absent:
```python
audit_path = ROOT / 'build/image4-ignition/aes-interface-audit.json'
recorded = ROOT / 'scripts/data/native-aes-original-bindings.S'
if not audit_path.is_file() and recorded.is_file():
    # Without the qualification evidence of the original kernelcache (kernel candidate, KDK
    # annotations, live metadata), bind with the recorded result of that audit. The addresses
    # belong to the kernelcache pinned in board.toml.
    ...
    print('PASS: native AES bound with the recorded original-kernelcache addresses')
```
That is why archive-06 passes and archive-10 does not.
## Proposed change
Either is fine; the first is preferred:
1. **Publish the record and add the same fallback.** Commit the audit as a pinned record (for example
   `scripts/data/storage-abi-interface-audit.json`) and let `build-virtio-mmio-bindings.py` read it
   when `build/storage-abi/interface-audit.json` is absent, with the same note: the addresses belong
   to the kernelcache pinned in `board.toml`. Note the builder already accepts a *missing*
   `native-apfs-load-positive.macho` ("the audit JSON is the pinned record"), so only the JSON has to
   be shipped.
2. **Document the staging.** If the record must stay unpublished, add the exact commands that
   produce it (candidate, QEMU fixture invocation, both snapshots, KDK version and kext hash) to the
   porting record and to the macOS workflow's `pre_build` documentation, so a contributor can
   reproduce it rather than guess.
The JSON contains only addresses, hashes, layout constants and booleans — no device identity — so
publishing it does not leak anything comparable to the platform seed.
## Workaround in use meanwhile
Disabling the native VirtIO/RAMBlock path and removing the two builder entries lets the kernel step
proceed:
```diff
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=y
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=y
-CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK_ARCHIVE="{tree}/build/virtio-mmio-block-verified-bundle/libVirtioMmioBlock.a"
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK=n
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_RAM_BLOCK=n
+CONFIG_XNU_NATIVE_VIRTIO_BLOCK_ARCHIVE=""
```
That is acceptable for real-hardware work (`ShengUfs` covers storage) but it removes the QEMU
storage-verification path, which is presumably the opposite of what you want tested in CI.
## Minor, same area
The missing-input case surfaces as a raw `FileNotFoundError` traceback instead of an `unixnu` error
with a hint. For an expected qualification gap, a clear message (like the platform-seed one) would
help — e.g. "no storage ABI qualification: run scripts/audit-storage-interface.py or provide the
recorded audit".

[unixnu-issue-storage-abi.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33962639/unixnu-issue-storage-abi.md)

issues.title: Stringsdict: all Russian plural entries are dropped on save, so the file is emptied and edits are never committed
issues.body:
### Describe the issue

On a **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`) component, saving the Russian translation writes an empty `<dict/>`. Every plural entry is dropped, including fully translated ones. The translations stay in the Weblate database, but they never reach the repository.

- File format: **Stringsdict file** (`stringsdict`), monolingual.
  - Base file: `<dir>/en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
  - File mask: `<dir>/*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`
- All entries are simple single-variable plurals (`NSStringLocalizedFormatKey` = `%#@count@`, one `NSStringPluralRuleType` dictionary).
- Add-ons on the component: `weblate.autotranslate.autotranslate`. The component is linked to the main component (`weblate://<project>/<component>`).
- Languages: de, es, fr, it, ja, ko, pt_BR, ru, zh_Hans, zh_Hant. **Only `ru` is affected.** The others save and commit normally.

What we observe:

1. A Weblate commit replaced our Russian file, which had 21 translated entries, with an empty dict:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
   <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
   <plist version="1.0">
   <dict/>
   </plist>
   ```
   The commit message was "Translated using Weblate (Russian) – Currently translated at 100.0%".
2. Since then, **Download translation → original format** gives the empty file above, while **Download → CSV** contains all Russian plural translations (it is generated from the database).
3. Editing a Russian string in the UI and committing produces no commit and no push. The written file is the same empty dict every time, so git has nothing to commit and no pull request is updated.

#### Root cause

The bug is in translate-toolkit's `StringsDictFile.serialize()` (`translate/storage/stringsdict.py`). It was introduced in translate-toolkit **3.19.19** by commit `3367ed4a` ("fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries"), which fixed #21294:

```python
plural_tags = self._get_target_plural_tags(unit.target)
...
# Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
# a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
if (
    "other" not in plural_tags
    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
):
    continue
```

`plural_tags` comes from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`. For `ru` (and also `pl`, `uk`, `be`) it is `["one", "few", "many"]`, and `_get_target_plural_tags()` adds `"zero"`, giving `['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']`. **`"other"` is never in that list, so the condition is always true and every entry is skipped,** however complete the translation is.

The previous serializer wrote these entries correctly. Our Russian file round-tripped through Weblate for over a year before this change.

#### Proposed fix (translate-toolkit)

For languages without an `other` category, use the last category as the required fallback:

```diff
--- a/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
+++ b/translate/storage/stringsdict.py
@@ -288,11 +288,11 @@ class StringsDictFile(base.DictStore):
 
                 # Omit an untranslated or incomplete entry instead of writing
-                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime.
-                if (
-                    "other" not in plural_tags
-                    or not plural_strings[plural_tags.index("other")]
-                ):
+                # a dictionary which Apple cannot resolve at runtime. Languages
+                # such as Russian have no integer "other" category, their last
+                # category is the fallback instead.
+                fallback_tag = "other" if "other" in plural_tags else plural_tags[-1]
+                if not plural_strings[plural_tags.index(fallback_tag)]:
                     continue
```

Regression test, in the style of the existing `tests/translate/storage/test_stringsdict.py`:

```python
def test_single_plural_without_other_category(self) -> None:
    content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>items</key>
    <dict>
        <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key>
        <string>%#@count@</string>
        <key>count</key>
        <dict>
            <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key>
            <string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
            <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key>
            <string>d</string>
            <key>one</key>
            <string>%d элемент</string>
            <key>few</key>
            <string>%d элемента</string>
            <key>many</key>
            <string>%d элементов</string>
        </dict>
    </dict>
</dict>
</plist>"""
    store = self.StoreClass()
    store.settargetlanguage("ru")
    store.parse(content.encode())

    assert store.units[0].target.strings == [
        "",
        "%d элемент",
        "%d элемента",
        "%d элементов",
    ]
    output = plistlib.loads(bytes(store))["items"]["count"]
    assert output["one"] == "%d элемент"
    assert output["many"] == "%d элементов"

    store.units[0].target = multistring(["", "%d элемент", "%d элемента", ""])
    assert plistlib.loads(bytes(store)) == {}
```

The last assertion keeps the intent of #21294: an entry whose fallback form is empty is still omitted.

An alternative would be to also emit an `other` key for these languages (CLDR uses `other` for fractional values in ru/pl/uk/be). That would change the number of plural forms shown in Weblate, so the change above is the minimal one.

#### Verified vs not verified

- Verified:
  - With translate-toolkit 3.20.1 (pinned by Weblate 2026.10.1), saving a translated Russian unit writes an empty dict.
  - The new test fails on unpatched code (`KeyError: 'items'`) and passes with the patch. The whole `test_stringsdict.py` suite passes (44 tests).
  - With the patched file installed in a `weblate==2026.10.1` environment, `StringsdictFormat` with our real `en` template and the empty `ru` file writes the Russian entry with its `one`, `few` and `many` forms.
  - translate-toolkit `main` at `888e46cc` (2026-10-29) still has the same check.
- Not verified:
  - Polish, Ukrainian and Belarusian; they are inferred from `translate.lang.data.plural_tags`.
  - The full Weblate test suite with the patch.
  - Apple runtime behaviour with a Russian dict without `other`. It worked in our app before 3.19.19.

### I already tried

- [x] I've read and searched [the documentation](https://docs.weblate.org/).
- [x] I've searched for similar filed issues in this repository.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

**In the UI**

1. Create a monolingual **Stringsdict file** component with base `en.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` and file mask `*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict`.
2. Add a Russian translation `ru.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict` with a complete simple plural entry (`one`/`few`/`many`). The **Standalone** example below has one.
3. Edit any Russian string in the editor and save.
4. Manage → Repository maintenance → Commit, or Files → Download translation (original format).
5. The Russian file is now `<dict/>`, and all entries are gone. After that, further Russian edits never produce a commit.

**Standalone (translate-toolkit only, no Weblate server)**

```python
# uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with "translate-toolkit==3.20.1" python repro.py
import plistlib
from translate.storage.stringsdict import StringsDictFile

content = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>items</key><dict>
    <key>NSStringLocalizedFormatKey</key><string>%#@count@</string>
    <key>count</key><dict>
      <key>NSStringFormatSpecTypeKey</key><string>NSStringPluralRuleType</string>
      <key>NSStringFormatValueTypeKey</key><string>d</string>
      <key>one</key><string>%d элемент</string>
      <key>few</key><string>%d элемента</string>
      <key>many</key><string>%d элементов</string>
    </dict>
  </dict>
</dict></plist>"""

store = StringsDictFile()
store.settargetlanguage("ru")
store.parse(content.encode())
print(store._get_target_plural_tags(store.units[0].target))  # ['zero', 'one', 'few', 'many']
print(plistlib.loads(bytes(store)))                          # {}  <- entry dropped
```

Changing `settargetlanguage("ru")` to `"de"` (with `one`/`other` keys) writes the entry correctly.

### Expected behavior

A complete Russian (or Polish, Ukrainian, Belarusian) plural entry is written to the file, as it was before translate-toolkit 3.19.19. Only an entry whose fallback form is empty should be omitted, which was the intent of #21294.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Exception traceback

```pytb

```

### How do you run Weblate?

weblate.org service

### Weblate version

2026.10.1 (translate-toolkit 3.20.1)

### Weblate deploy checks

```shell

```

### Additional context

- Introduced by translate-toolkit commit `3367ed4a` "fix(stringsdict): fold simple plural entries", released in **3.19.19** (2026-09-01) and present in 3.20.0, 3.20.1 and `main`. It was a follow-up to #21294.
- The wrong language data is in `translate/lang/data.py` → `plural_tags["ru"] == ["one", "few", "many"]` (same for `pl`, `uk`, `be`). `DECIMAL_EXTRA_TAGS` in the same file lists `other` for these languages, but `_get_target_plural_tags()` doesn't use it.
- Impact: every Russian translation edit made in Weblate is silently kept out of the repository, and the first such commit wipes the existing Russian file. The only workaround is to maintain the Russian `.stringsdict` directly in the repository and avoid editing Russian in Weblate.
- Related: #21294.

issues.title: Download succeeds but request returns 500 when the torrent URL redirects to a magnet link
issues.body:
## Environment

- AudioBookRequest v1.10.5, official Docker image `markbeep/audiobookrequest:1`
- Prowlarr 2.x with torrent indexers (observed with a Knaben result whose grab resolves to a RuTracker magnet)

## Symptom

Starting a download returns HTTP 500 to the user even though the grab itself succeeded: Prowlarr accepts the release and the torrent shows up in the download client. Because the handler dies mid-way, the book is never marked downloaded, no success notification is sent, and the ABS scan is not triggered.

## What happens

After a successful grab, `start_download` fetches the source's `download_url` to extract the torrent info hash for notification metadata (`app/internal/prowlarr/prowlarr.py:123`, calling `_get_torrent_info_hash` at `prowlarr.py:39`). For some indexers, Prowlarr's proxied download URL responds with a redirect to a `magnet:` URI. aiohttp refuses to follow non-HTTP redirects and raises, and the exception propagates out of the whole request:

```
File "/app/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/aiohttp/client.py", line 878, in _request
    raise NonHttpUrlRedirectClientError(r_url)
aiohttp.client_exceptions.NonHttpUrlRedirectClientError: magnet:?xt=urn:btih:<infohash-redacted>&tr=http%3A%2F%2Fbt.t-ru.org%2Fann%3Fmagnet
```

Note the irony: the info hash the code wanted is right there in the magnet URI it crashed on.

## Reproduction

1. Add an indexer whose torrent downloads resolve to magnet redirects (e.g. Knaben results that proxy RuTracker items).
2. Request a book and start a download for such a source.
3. The torrent is added to the download client, but the request returns 500 and the book stays "not downloaded".

## Suggested direction

- In `_get_torrent_info_hash`, request with `allow_redirects=False`; if the response is a redirect to a `magnet:` URI, parse the info hash from it (the same parsing already exists for `magnet_url` sources at `prowlarr.py:127-131`).
- Regardless, wrap the metadata fetch in a try/except so a failure to enrich notification metadata can never fail a download that already succeeded.

Would you take a PR where the on-TV app's Keep watching also lists Watch Next rows directly when it has that permission, the same way the TV home app does? I'm happy to write it and test it on the stick.

issues.body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Providers

### Apache Airflow version

main (development)

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

With an SSH `repo_url`, `GitDagBundle.view_url_template()` removes `.git` from anywhere in the repository name, not just the end. The Dag source link in the UI, and `bundle_url` in the REST API, then point to a repository that doesn't exist. The HTTPS form of the same URL gives the correct link.

```python
from airflow.providers.git.bundles.git import GitDagBundle

bundle = GitDagBundle(name="dags", tracking_ref="main", repo_url="git@github.com:apache/airflow.github.io.git")
print(bundle.view_url_template())
# https://github.com/apache/airflowhub.io/tree/{version}
```

### What you think should happen instead?

Only a trailing `.git` should be stripped, as it already is for HTTPS URLs: `https://github.com/apache/airflow.github.io/tree/{version}`. The cause is `parts[1].replace(".git", "")` in `GitDagBundle._convert_git_ssh_url_to_https`.

issues.title: Maximise app performance: startup, inference, memory, long jobs, UI, install, energy, mobile
issues.body:
Tracking issue: make VoiceStudio measurably faster and lighter across every dimension users feel, on macOS, Windows and Linux (and phones). Each item lands as a focused PR with a before/after number. No regression in output quality or cross-platform behaviour (CLAUDE.md parity rule: acceleration may vary by host, features may not).

## Dimensions

**1. App startup**
- [ ] Measure cold and warm time to first paint and to "backend ready" on each OS
- [ ] Lazy-load heavy routes and engines; defer non-critical IPC and checks until after first paint
- [ ] Trim the backend's import-time work (`_phase_a_build_inner`) and import routers on demand

**2. Inference throughput and latency**
- [ ] Per-engine benchmark (time to first audio, real-time factor) on CUDA, MPS, ROCm, Vulkan and CPU
- [ ] Keep models warm between takes; avoid redundant reloads on settings changes
- [ ] Stream the first chunk early for TTS and dictation; batch chunks where engines allow
- [ ] Use fp16/bf16, quantised (GGUF) and `torch.compile` paths where the host supports them, skipped cleanly where not

**3. Memory (RAM and VRAM)**
- [ ] Profile peak RAM and VRAM per engine and per pipeline (dub, long-form, batch)
- [ ] Unload idle engines and free caches under memory pressure; one engine resident by default
- [ ] Stop holding long audio fully in memory; stream to disk

**4. Long jobs (dubbing, audiobooks, 50-video batches)**
- [ ] Pipeline overlap: ASR, translation and TTS stages run concurrently where safe
- [ ] Resume from the last finished segment after a crash or restart
- [ ] Bounded parallelism tuned to the device instead of fixed

**5. UI responsiveness**
- [ ] Renderer bundle size budget and code splitting; track it in CI
- [ ] Virtualise long lists (history, voices, projects, gallery)
- [ ] Keep the main and renderer threads free: no sync IPC or heavy work on render paths
- [ ] Interaction latency budget (e.g. < 100 ms for clicks) checked by the UI crawler

**6. Install, update and disk**
- [ ] Smaller installers and runtime (prune unused wheels and assets)
- [ ] Faster first-run setup: parallel downloads within the sanctioned endpoints, better resume
- [ ] Differential updates where the updater supports them
- [ ] Shared model caches without duplicates; show and clean disk use

**7. Energy and thermals**
- [ ] Idle CPU near zero: no polling loops while idle; back off background checks
- [ ] Battery-aware defaults on laptops

**8. Mobile (on-device)**
- [ ] On-device model load time and memory on mid-range Android and iPhone
- [ ] Quantised on-device models; keep the UI at 60 fps during generation

## Measurement
- [ ] Add a reproducible benchmark script (`scripts/bench/`) with fixed inputs, run per platform
- [ ] Record baselines for the current release in this issue, then compare each PR against them
- [ ] Add CI perf smoke checks for startup time, bundle size and idle CPU, with alert thresholds that don't block merges on noise

## Rules
- Local-first unchanged: no new network calls for telemetry. Opt-in Supermetry analytics may carry coarse, content-free timing only if allowlisted in `backend/core/analytics.py`.
- No output-quality regressions: fixed-seed audio comparisons for engine changes.
- On-disk model state stays compatible (no forced reinstalls).

issues.title: chore(tooling): review the S110 waivers in the expert scripts
issues.body:
PR #371 turns on ruff S110: an `except` (bare, `Exception` or `BaseException`) whose body is only `pass` fails `pnpm lint:py`. A swallowed error lets a run report success.

The expert scripts that predate the rule keep a per-file waiver in `ruff.toml`, with their count of hits. This issue tracks removing them.

## Per site

- Fix it: catch the narrowest exception, then log, re-raise, or record the failure in the result.
- Or keep it: add `# noqa: S110` and the reason on the `except` line, when the host application's error is safe to ignore there.
- A comment beside the `pass` does not satisfy S110.

- Remove the file's `[lint.per-file-ignores]` entry once every clause is fixed or carries a reason.

issues.title: Notes batch actions report full success after rejected archive/delete requests
issues.body:
AI-assisted bug report, reproduced against unchanged public dev `0276e15f6e2e7a4a692d130243f2a02c3f57ffe0` before implementing a fix.

### Environment

Native macOS/Python 3.12/Uvicorn/SQLite, authenticated disposable account; Chrome at 1440×1000 and 390×844. No model inference, API response interception or DOM replacements.

### Reproduction

1. Create three owned notes. Enter Notes → Select, select all three and click Archive or Delete (confirm deletion).
2. Make the server reject just the middle note's mutation. I used a SQLite trigger in the disposable database to raise ABORT for that owned ID: `BEFORE DELETE ON notes`, or `BEFORE UPDATE OF archived ON notes WHEN NEW.archived=1`. The three actual HTTP responses are 200, 500, 200.
3. Observe the completion message, remaining note and selection.
4. For the same batch handling in reminder clearing, create three notes with past timed `due_date` values. Choose the Reminders filter and Clear past, confirming deletion, with the same middle-note rejection.

### Actual / expected

The app reports `Archived 3`, `Deleted 3` or `Cleared 3 past reminders`, shows no error and, for bulk selection, exits Select and clears the failed note's selection. The server correctly retains that note; only two operations succeeded. Failed items should be reported, successes counted accurately and failed selected notes kept available for retry.

Clearing the owned trigger allows a normal retry to succeed. This is client response handling, not a request to alter backend mutation/ownership rules. Individual note-delete error handling is a separate existing path.

### Source

`frontend/src/features/notes/application/selection.js` catches each rejected archive/delete request and then always reports the original count and exits selection. `application/deletion.js::_clearPastReminders` similarly ignores delete failures and claims every target was cleared. The deployed copies match.

### Duplicate checks

Searched open/closed issues and PRs for Notes bulk failures, rejected archive/delete, partial failure and clearing past reminders. No equivalent active fix found. Gallery draft-delete reporting and Skills rejected-write handling affect separate workflows; neither changes these Notes batch handlers.

issues.title: Inkling: BF16 router rounds distinct scores into ties before Top-K
issues.body:
`InklingTopkRouter` performs sigmoid and correction-bias addition in BF16 after `from_pretrained(..., dtype=torch.bfloat16)`. Distinct scores can become ties **before** Top-K, changing expert selection without producing NaNs. BF16 autocast also exposes this with FP32 model weights.

### System Info

- Transformers `5.23.0.dev0`, commit [b2556881](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/commit/b25568817a6cb458f6d8b180a32698c2ab11fd26)
- Python 3.12.13, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`; reproduced on CPU and NVIDIA RTX A1000 Laptop GPU.
- Affected code: [InklingTopkRouter.forward](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/b25568817a6cb458f6d8b180a32698c2ab11fd26/src/transformers/models/inkling/modeling_inkling.py#L359-L379).

### Reproduction

No checkpoint download is needed. The logits below are exactly representable in BF16; the assertion excludes GEMM rounding as the cause.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import InklingTextConfig
from transformers.models.inkling.modeling_inkling import InklingTopkRouter

device = "cpu"  # Also reproduces on CUDA.
config = InklingTextConfig(
    hidden_size=2, n_routed_experts=8, n_shared_experts=2,
    num_experts_per_tok=2,
)
router = InklingTopkRouter(config).to(device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
with torch.no_grad():
    router.weight.zero_()
    router.weight[:8, 0].copy_(
        torch.tensor([6.25, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8, 8.5, 9, 10], device=device)
    )
x = torch.tensor([[1., 0.]], device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
logits = F.linear(x, router.weight)
assert torch.equal(logits.float(), F.linear(x.float(), router.weight.float()))

print("BF16 scores:", logits.sigmoid()[0, :8].tolist())
print("Actual:", router(x)[2].sort().values.tolist())
for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
    scores = logits.to(dtype).sigmoid()[:, :8]
    print(dtype, scores.topk(2, sorted=False).indices.sort().values.tolist())
```

All eight BF16 sigmoid scores are `1.0`. Observed expert **sets**:

| Device | Current BF16 router | FP32 / FP64 sigmoid |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | `{5, 6}` | `{6, 7}` |
| CUDA | `{0, 1}` | `{6, 7}` |

Tie-breaking can vary; losing the distinct scores is the issue.

I also reproduced the loading path with a small three-layer `InklingForCausalLM` through `save_pretrained → from_pretrained(dtype=bfloat16)`. On CPU, switching to FP32 routing changed expert sets for 19/48 tokens while loss changed by only about `4.8e-7`; logits and gradients remained finite. This is a synthetic test, not a full-model quality measurement.

### Expected behavior

Preserve FP32 routing decisions, consistent with [SGLang's FP32-output gate projection](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/96f013b45202cabd8d4a0d6e79596f109538181e/python/sglang/srt/models/inkling_common/moe.py#L66-L120).

The locally tested fix needs three parts:

1. Disable autocast around FP32 projection, sigmoid, bias addition and normalization. Casting linear inputs/weights to `float()` alone still produces BF16 output under BF16 autocast.
2. Add `e_score_correction_bias` and `gate.global_scale` to `_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict`. Loading currently rounds both to BF16; casting afterward cannot recover their values. Scope the scale entry to `gate` because dense MLPs have a same-named parameter.
3. Cast the final routing coefficients back to the hidden-state dtype, so the shared experts' BF16 down-projection remains compatible.

This approach passed CPU/CUDA forward/backward checks for BF16, BF16+AMP and FP32+AMP, plus exact FP32 bias/scale preservation across saving and loading.

Thanks for taking the time to review this. I'd appreciate your feedback on the diagnosis and proposed approach. I'll wait for your guidance before opening a PR, and I'd be happy to contribute the fix and regression tests.

- `transformers` 5.23.0.dev0 (main @ `863d2620210d72fc0a9a03fdfe200bc9699154f6`)
- `torch` 2.12.1+cu130, Python 3.13, Linux x86_64

### Description

For 11 model families, a model built from its **default config** (`XConfig()`) either fails during `__init__` or builds but can never run a forward pass. The causes are a required field left as `None`, or two sub-config dimensions that disagree. Loading from the Hub works, because the checkpoint configs set these fields. The failures only show up when a model is built from the default config, as in tests, tiny-model construction, or `from_config` with partial overrides.

We found these while running every model class through `torch.compile` from default configs. As far as we could tell, none of them is tracked by an existing issue or PR. A related earlier case of the same kind: #43479 (Phi4Multimodal) and #42925 (TVP `type_vocab_size`).

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
import transformers as t

def build(model_cls, cfg_cls):
    try:
        cfg = getattr(t, cfg_cls)()
        with torch.device("meta"):
            getattr(t, model_cls)(cfg)
        return "OK"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:110]}"

for m, c in [
    ("CohereCompassModel", "CohereCompassConfig"),
    ("DiffusionGemmaModel", "DiffusionGemmaConfig"),
    ("DeepseekOcr2Model", "DeepseekOcr2Config"),
    ("Granite4VisionModel", "Granite4VisionConfig"),
    ("HunYuanVLModel", "HunYuanVLConfig"),
    ("MoshiForConditionalGeneration", "MoshiConfig"),
    ("PPOCRV6MediumDetModel", "PPOCRV6MediumDetConfig"),
    ("Qwen4ExpModel", "Qwen4ExpConfig"),
]:
    print(f"[build] {m}: {build(m, c)}")

c = t.Qwen3ASRConfig()
print(f"[dims] Qwen3ASR audio_config.output_dim={c.audio_config.output_dim} "
      f"text_config.hidden_size={c.text_config.hidden_size}")
c = t.Molmo2Config()
print(f"[dims] Molmo2 adapter_config.text_hidden_size={c.adapter_config.text_hidden_size} "
      f"text_config.hidden_size={c.text_config.hidden_size}")
c = t.Step3p7TextConfig()
print(f"[fwd] Step3p7 sliding_window={c.sliding_window} layer_types={sorted(set(c.layer_types))}")
```

Output:

```
[build] CohereCompassModel: KeyError: 'full_attention'
[build] DiffusionGemmaModel: TypeError: empty() received an invalid combination of arguments - got (tuple, dtype=NoneType, device=NoneType), but expec
[build] DeepseekOcr2Model: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
[build] Granite4VisionModel: TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
[build] HunYuanVLModel: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for ** or pow(): 'NoneType' and 'float'
[build] MoshiForConditionalGeneration: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'
[build] PPOCRV6MediumDetModel: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
[build] Qwen4ExpModel: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for //: 'NoneType' and 'NoneType'
[dims] Qwen3ASR audio_config.output_dim=3584 text_config.hidden_size=2048
[dims] Molmo2 adapter_config.text_hidden_size=3584 text_config.hidden_size=4096
[fwd] Step3p7 sliding_window=None layer_types=['full_attention']
```

### Per-model details

Where a public reference checkpoint exists, the value it uses is listed for comparison.

**A. The default config can't build the model**

| Model | Field left unset by the default | Where it fails | Reference checkpoint value |
|---|---|---|---|
| CohereCompass | `text_config.rope_parameters` defaults to `{}` with all-`full_attention` `layer_types`. The rotary init indexes `rope_parameters[layer_type]`. | `CohereCompassRotaryEmbedding.__init__` → `KeyError: 'full_attention'` | `CohereLabs/North-Micro-Vision-Instruct`: `{"sliding_attention": {...}, "full_attention": null}`, with mixed sliding/full layer types |
| DiffusionGemma | `text_config.num_experts`, `top_k_experts`, `moe_intermediate_size` are `None` | `DiffusionGemmaTextRouter`: `nn.Linear(hidden, None)` | `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`: 128 / 8 / 704 |
| DeepseekOcr2 | `text_config.mlp_layer_types` is `None` (also `n_group`, `topk_group`, `num_experts_per_tok`) | `DeepseekOcr2TextDecoderLayer.__init__`: `config.mlp_layer_types[layer_idx]` | `deepseek-community/DeepSeek-OCR-2`: `["dense"] + ["sparse"] * 11`, `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `num_experts_per_tok=6` |
| Granite4Vision | `deepstack_layer_map` is `None` | `Granite4VisionModel.__init__`: `len(config.deepstack_layer_map)` | `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-3b-vision`: `[[-19, 9], [-13, 6], [-7, 3], [-1, 0]]`. Note that the `auto_docstring` checkpoint for this config points to `llava-hf/llava-v1.6-mistral-7b-hf`, which looks wrong. |
| HunYuanVL | `text_config.head_dim` is `None` | `HunYuanVLDenseV1Attention.__init__`: `self.head_dim**-0.5`. The config applies a `hidden_size // num_attention_heads` fallback in one place, but the attention module doesn't use it. | n/a (no `auto_docstring` checkpoint) |
| Moshi | top-level `audio_vocab_size` is `None` | `nn.Embedding(config.audio_vocab_size + 1, ...)`. This worked on 5.5.x, so it is a regression. | `kmhf/hf-moshika`: 2048 |
| PPOCRV6MediumDet | `intraclass_block_config` is `None` | `PPOCRV6MediumDetIntraclassBlock.__init__`: `intraclass_block_config["reduce_channel"]` | `PaddlePaddle/PP-OCRv6_medium_det_safetensors` (full dict in `config.json`) |
| Qwen4Exp | every `indexer_*` field is `None`, but each `indexed_attention` layer builds a `Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer` regardless | `Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer.__init__`: `token_budget // compress_ratio` | `Qwen/Qwen4-Exp` is gated, so we couldn't check |

**B. The model builds, but a forward pass can never succeed**

| Model | Inconsistency | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3ASR | `audio_config.output_dim=3584` but `text_config.hidden_size=2048` | The projector output is `masked_scatter`ed into the text embeddings, and `get_placeholder_mask` fails its numel check ("Audio features and audio tokens do not match, tokens: N, features: N") even when token counts match. |
| Molmo2 | `adapter_config.text_hidden_size=3584` but `text_config.hidden_size=4096` | Pooled image features are added onto the placeholder embeddings, and the numel check in `get_placeholder_mask` fails. |
| Step3p7 | `sliding_window=None`, and the default `layer_types` are all `full_attention` | `Step3p7TextModel.forward` always builds `create_sliding_window_causal_mask(...)` (`modeling_step3p7.py:892`), even when no layer uses sliding attention. This raises `ValueError: Could not find a sliding_window argument in the config, or it is not set`. |

### Expected behavior

`XModel(XConfig())` builds, and runs a forward pass on valid inputs, for every model class.

issues.title: finegrained_fp8 models are silently mis-dequantized when loaded on CPU if a quantized weight has partial blocks
issues.body:
### System Info ```text - transformers version: 5.22.1 - Platform: Linux-5.x-x86_64 (CPU-only) - Python version: 3.12.15 - Huggingface_hub version: 2.4.0 - Safetensors version: 0.8.0 - Accelerate version: 1.15.0 - PyTorch version: 2.15.0+cpu (CPU build) - CUDA/GPU: none — CPU-only host, which is exactly the forced-dequantize path ``` The same wrongness is bit-identical on transformers 5.17.0 (checked at the `Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one` level), and the relevant code is unchanged on current `main` (source-checked 2026-11-11: the equal-division derivation at ~L1152, the loud `ValueError` at ~L1148, and the partial-aware `_dequantize_fp8_weight` helper at ~L285 all coexist). ### Who can help? @SunMarc @MekkCyber (quantization) ### Reproduction Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. On a host **without GPU/XPU**, load a finegrained_fp8 checkpoint (`quant_method: "fp8"`, the DeepSeek checkpoint family) whose quantized linear weights have partial 128-blocks — i.e. any hidden/intermediate dimension that is not a multiple of `weight_block_size` (external per-block quantization tooling emits such ceil-shaped grids by construction). 2. transformers forces `dequantize=True` ("Using FP8 quantized models requires a GPU or XPU, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16 since no GPU or XPU is available"), and `Fp8Dequantize` derives the block size from the scale grid **by equal division** (`block_m = rows // scale_rows`), while the format's semantics are ceil grids with partial edge blocks. 3. The load **succeeds silently** and the weights are wrong. On a GPU host the same checkpoint loads correctly (the quantized path's own `_dequantize_fp8_weight` is partial-block aware). Self-contained script (tiny locally generated Llama checkpoints in the DeepSeek fp8 format, no downloads; the same script is archived next to this issue as `issue-reproducer.py`): [issue-reproducer.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34669945/issue-reproducer.py) ```python import json import os import tempfile import warnings from pathlib import Path warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1") import torch from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM from transformers.integrations.finegrained_fp8 import ( Fp8Dequantize, _dequantize_fp8_weight, ) BLOCK, FP8_MAX = (128, 128), 448.0 def quantize_reference(w): """Quantize per the format's reference semantics (ceil grids).""" rows, cols = w.shape grid_r, grid_c = (rows + 127) // 128, (cols + 127) // 128 codes = torch.zeros_like(w) scales = torch.zeros(grid_r, grid_c) deq = torch.zeros_like(w) for i in range(grid_r): for j in range(grid_c): sl = (slice(i * 128, (i + 1) * 128), slice(j * 128, (j + 1) * 128)) mult = w[sl].abs().max().clamp(min=1e-12) / FP8_MAX codes[sl] = torch.clamp(w[sl] / mult, -FP8_MAX, FP8_MAX) scales[i, j] = mult # post-round truth: what any consumer reads back from the checkpoint deq[sl] = codes[sl].to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float() * mult return codes.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), scales, deq def build_checkpoint(root, hidden): torch.manual_seed(0) cfg = LlamaConfig(hidden_size=hidden, intermediate_size=512, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=4, vocab_size=128, max_position_embeddings=256, tie_word_embeddings=False, architectures=["LlamaForCausalLM"]) model = LlamaForCausalLM(cfg).to(torch.bfloat16) tensors, ground, qnames = {}, {}, [] for name, t in model.state_dict().items(): if name != "lm_head.weight" and any(s in name for s in ("q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")): codes, scales, deq = quantize_reference(t.float()) prefix = name[: -len(".weight")] tensors[name], tensors[prefix + ".weight_scale_inv"] = codes, scales tensors[prefix + ".activation_scale"] = torch.tensor(1.0) ground[name] = deq qnames.append(name) else: tensors[name], ground[name] = t.detach().clone(), t d = root / f"ckpt-h{hidden}" d.mkdir(parents=True) save_file(tensors, str(d / "model.safetensors")) cd = cfg.to_dict() cd["quantization_config"] = {"quant_method": "fp8", "activation_scheme": "dynamic", "weight_block_size": [128, 128]} cd["torch_dtype"] = "bfloat16" (d / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(cd, indent=2, sort_keys=True)) return d, ground, qnames def load_and_compare(ckpt, ground, qnames): model = LlamaForCausalLM.from_pretrained(str(ckpt), torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) sd = model.state_dict() bad = 0 for n in qnames: bad += int((sd[n].float() - ground[n].to(torch.bfloat16).float()).abs().gt(0).sum()) return bad def main(): with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td: root = Path(td) # control: every linear dim divisible by the 128 block d, g, q = build_checkpoint(root, 256) print("hidden 256 (divisible): wrong elements =", load_and_compare(d, g, q)) # defect: hidden 200 -> partial row blocks, grid (2, .), 200 % 2 == 0 d, g, q = build_checkpoint(root, 200) print("hidden 200 (partial): wrong elements =", load_and_compare(d, g, q)) # mechanism: the same codes+scales through both in-repo implementations t = load_file(str(d / "model.safetensors")) qn = next(n for n in q if n.endswith("q_proj.weight")) p = qn[: -len(".weight")] class _Q: class quantization_config: scale_fmt = "float" cpu = Fp8Dequantize(_Q())._dequantize_one(t[qn], t[p + ".weight_scale_inv"], output_dtype=torch.float32) helper = _dequantize_fp8_weight(t[qn], t[p + ".weight_scale_inv"], [128, 128], torch.float32) gt = g[qn] print("q_proj (200, 200), grid (2, 2):") print(" Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one (CPU load path): max diff", float((cpu - gt).abs().max())) print(" _dequantize_fp8_weight (partial-aware): max diff", float((helper - gt).abs().max())) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Actual output (transformers 5.22.1, CPU-only host): ```text [transformers] Using FP8 quantized models requires a GPU or XPU, we will default to dequantizing the model to bf16 since no GPU or XPU is available hidden 256 (divisible): wrong elements = 0 hidden 200 (partial): wrong elements = 168915 q_proj (200, 200), grid (2, 2): Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one (CPU load path): max diff 0.0129743292927742 _dequantize_fp8_weight (partial-aware): max diff 0.0 ``` All 14 quantized tensors of the `hidden_size=200` model are wrong (each 200×200 tensor has 10416/40000 wrong elements): rows 100–127 fall into the second derived block (100 rows each) although the quantizer's blocks were `[0:128] + [128:200]`, so they are dequantized with the wrong per-block scale. A second variant — a dimension whose size does not divide by its grid count — fails loudly instead (also wrong: the reference consumer loads such checkpoints fine):
ValueError from _dequantize_one (e.g. intermediate_size=131, weight (256, 131), grid (2, 2)) ```text File ".../transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py", line 1149, in _dequantize_one raise ValueError( ValueError: Weight shape (256, 131) not divisible by scale grid (2, 2). ```
Reference semantics for `weight_scale_inv` grids (why the above checkpoint is legal): vLLM's fp8 utils dequantizes with `repeat_interleave(block, ...)[:_N, :_K]` (partial-block aware), and transformers' own `_dequantize_fp8_weight` — used by the quantized path's backward in the same file — truncates `[..., :rows, :]` and handles a `rem` branch. Only the CPU forced-dequantize path assumes equal blocks. ### Expected behavior Loading the same fp8 checkpoint on a CPU-only host should produce the same weights as on a GPU host. Concretely, `Fp8Dequantize._dequantize_one` should apply the ceil-grid block semantics grid cell `i` covers rows `[i*128, min((i+1)*128, rows)]` — exactly what `_dequantize_fp8_weight` already implements — instead of `block_m = rows // scale_rows`; and a scale grid inconsistent with `ceil(rows / weight_block_size[0])` should fail loudly rather than being reinterpreted by an arbitrary factorization (the current code accepts any grid that divides the shape, e.g. a `(1, 4)` grid for a 256×256 weight would silently use 64-column blocks).

issues.title: [Bug] OnlineDSpineModel uses stale config after draft config replacement
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues.
- [x] The bug is present on the latest main checked.
- [x] Environment details are filled in below.

### Describe the bug

`OnlineDSpineModel` stores `draft_model.dspine_config` at construction. `DSpineConfig` is frozen, so replacing the draft's config afterwards leaves the online model using the old values without warning. For example, attempts to disable predecessor replacement and alignment warmup can leave them active. Constructing the online model after setting the config works.

### Reproduction

From a SpecForge checkout with its test dependencies installed, run this CPU example using the existing tiny-model test helper:

```python
from dataclasses import replace
from tests.test_modeling.test_dspine import training_model

model = training_model()
draft = model.draft_model
draft.dspine_config = replace(
    draft.dspine_config, replacement_probability=0.0, alignment_warmup_steps=0
)
print(draft.dspine_config.replacement_probability)  # 0.0
print(model.dspine_config.replacement_probability)  # 0.5: expected 0.0
print(model.dspine_config.alignment_warmup_steps)  # 146: expected 0
```

The issue also affects fine-tuning `tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16`. Consider a property that reads `self.draft_model.dspine_config`, or reject a mismatch explicitly. Structural config changes may require rebuilding draft submodules; the intended supported updates should be validated separately.

Related: #1038 (DSpine objective), and a similar silent-default report in a review on #1160.

### Environment

Reproduced on CPU at main `224b36bd` and PR #1038 head `2dadea10` (on the latter the warm-up prints `None`, the PR's new default). Current main `132d35d3` has the same code. Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu132, Transformers 5.21.0.dev0, Linux x86_64.

issues.title: [建议] 孩子档案的教材版本缺五四制选项（青岛版/鲁教版/鲁科版），建议再区分学制
issues.body:
## 想解决什么问题

档案的「教材版本」只有 人教版/北师大版/苏教版/沪教版/外研版/译林版/其他，山东**五四学制**地区（烟台、威海、泰安、东营、济南莱芜区等）的孩子没有对应选项，只能选「其他」，档案卡显示成「二年级 · 其他」。

据烟台市教育局 2026-07-08《烟台市义务教育阶段教辅材料推荐选用结果公示》（教材版本 / 学制两列，均标五四）：小学数学=青岛版，小学英语=鲁科版，初中数学=鲁教版，初中英语=鲁教版，初中物理=鲁科版，初中化学=鲁教版，初中生物=鲁科版，语文与道德与法治=人教版（统编）。

## 更深一层：年级标签是按六三制排的

`grade`/`semester` 是人教版·六三制编排（小学 1–6 年级 12 册，七年级=初一；README 也写明「六三制化学在九年级开设，不采用五四制全一册」）。五四制小学只有 1–5 年级、六年级已进初中，单元次序不同，所以五四制用户按「年级」列对照实际进度会偏；按知识点 + 先修边回溯根因是可靠的。

## 建议方案

1. `TEXTBOOKS` 增加 `青岛版（五四制）`、`鲁教版（五四制）`、`鲁科版（五四制）`，`clean()` 白名单同步。
2. 档案再加「学制」字段（六三制 / 五四制），与教材版本分开——同一版本名在两个学制下册次不同。
3. 诊断页/图谱页年级筛选处提示「本图谱按人教版·六三制编排，五四制请按知识点而非年级对照」；若做换算，大致是 五四制六年级 ≈ 六三制七年级（需逐册核对，别写死）。
4. `validate.py` 与 `tests/test_children*.js` 里涉及 `TEXTBOOKS` 的断言同步。

issues.title: 科学子图节点教材锚定异常：7 幻点+2 描述失真+1 挪位（教科版 2024 版实拍取证）
issues.body:
感谢维护。我们用国家中小学智慧教育平台官方电子课本（教科版 2024 修订版 12 册，版次已核：一上版权页 2024 年 7 月第 1 版）对 science 子图（cns_p001-p222）做了逐册目录对账＋疑点页实拍，发现三类锚定异常，均附逐字证据（页码）：

## 1. 无教材锚节点 7 个（2017/2024 版目录均无对应课）
植物的根、茎、叶 / 物体是用什么做的 / 动物的身体特征 / 牢固的结构 / 化石是怎样形成的（内容疑源自课标 css-2022 条目自建）；磁铁的两极 / 磁铁在生活中的应用（2017 版课名残留，2024 版已删，两极内容移三下「磁极与方向」）。

## 2. 描述与教材内容不符 2 个
- 动物联欢会（一下 U2）：官方课为扮演活动（制作头饰/表演/交流，实拍 p44-45），图谱写「按生活环境、身体特征给动物分类」；
- 让小车动起来（二下 U2）：2024 版为磁力隔空驱动＋距离影响，图谱写「同极相斥、异极相吸」（2017 版「磁极间的相互作用」语义）。

## 3. 学序挪位 1 个
观察云（三上）：教材=U1-6 印 17-18（页眉「6 观察云」实拍可证），图谱把它排在「水珠从哪里来」（印 33）之后，依赖方向与教材学序相反。

另：2024 版二下 U2 顺序为 磁铁能吸引什么→比较力量的大小→让小车动起来→隔物吸铁→设计钓鱼玩具→我们来钓鱼，与现图谱顺序不一致。

## 根因线索
`scripts/sci_edges.py` 的 hard() 表直接定义了上述内容点概念（如 g1a_genjing/g1b_dongwutezheng/g3a_yun 的机制先修断言），这些概念在 2024 教材中无独立课时载体；观察云的先修断言（「理解云的组成，要先知道水蒸气遇冷凝结」）在印 17-18 正文中亦无对应教学内容。

## 建议
建点闸加「教材锚」字段（册/课/页）防版本混杂；上述节点按 2024 版归位/合并/删除。证据包（含 12 册目录逐字转写与实拍页）可提供。我们在本地 pin 仓已做数据层修正（并 2 删 5、[78] 翻向等），因数据为流水线产物、PR 会被下次生成覆盖，故以 Issue 报告根因。

issues.title: Feature Requests - Vapor pressure sensor
issues.body:
This is a very important sensor value, when growing plants. 

WPD of the leaves tell you about the resperation of the plant.

VPD = VPleaf - VPair
VPleaf = 610.7 * 107.5*Tleaf/(237.3+Tleaf) / 1000
VPair = 610.7 * 107.5*Tair/(237.3+Tair)/1000 * RH/100

VPleaf - vapor pressure of the leaf (canopy) in kPa
VPair - vapor pressure of the air in kPa
Tleaf - leaf temperature in Celsius
Tair - air temperature in Celsius
RH - air relative humidity
VPD - vapor pressure deficit in kPa

Or simply, use the a chart [VPD chart and calculator](https://vpdchart.com/).
You need a thermometer/hygrometer to measure the grow room temperature, RH and ideally an [infrared thermometer](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=ir+thermometer&sprefix=ir+t%2Caps%2C172&linkCode=ll2&tag=vpdchart-20&linkId=8f866cae94fbf85ace5190dfc1d502da&language=en_US&ref_=as_li_ss_tl), so you can measure the canopy temperature. If you don't have an infrared thermometer, position your thermometer's remote probe at canopy level and take the reading after a few minutes, or assume that leaf temperature is 2°C cooler than air temperature.

In depth PDF article: 
[https://journals.ametsoc.org/downloadpdf/journals/apme/6/1/1520-0450_1967_006_0203_otcosv_2_0_co_2.xml](https://journals.ametsoc.org/downloadpdf/journals/apme/6/1/1520-0450_1967_006_0203_otcosv_2_0_co_2.xml)
